finding: The gates are per clinic, but the pillar ships first and claims WorkSafeBC physiotherapy 'at 19+ clinics' in its title, meta and hero. Its finder gives all 19 clinics 'Book WCB assessment' links, including Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners, which are HIGH risk and held to Wave 3 until Q-1. Band 3 says 'pending G1', but G1 is undefined for the pillar, and Q-1 says it blocks 'any page'. So either the whole program waits on all 19 contracts, or the pillar publishes the exact unverified claim the gates exist to stop.
recommendation: Derive the pillar from clinic gates. The finder lists only G1-true clinics; any count is computed from them or dropped from title, meta and hero; billing wording stays at WorkSafeBC's general rule (WSBC-11). Write this into §4 so the pillar depends only on the Wave 1 clinics.

finding: Hand-pasted static Elementor fragments copy each clinic's NAP and hours into the pillar finder, its own page, sibling nearby blocks and JSON-LD. NAP edits are certain (G2 is open for all 19 clinics; at least 8 are unresolved), and each one means re-pasting several pages by hand. The repo stops being the source of truth after the first edit in WordPress. The gates exist only in the build, so nothing stops someone pasting a preview fragment or editing a claim after paste. The content team cannot edit HTML widgets. The repo's existing data-to-WordPress path (collect.js pushing to the data branch, rendered server-side by the Synergy Availability plugin with shortcodes and in-shortcode CSS enqueue) is never considered, and Alternatives weighs no delivery option.
recommendation: Add a delivery alternative and decide it. Either author the Wave 1 pages in WordPress with the stylesheet and a saved template, postponing any generator until Wave 2; or render the clinic-data parts through a shortcode in the existing plugin, fed by the JSON, with G1 and G2 checked at render time.

finding: merge_locations.py regenerates worksafe-locations.json with staff_facts null and publish_gates hard-coded, overwriting the file. CUJ 4 has marketing set gates in that same file, so re-running the merge (needed to refresh the dated Jane data) wipes all sign-offs and staff facts. Human inputs are also spread over staff-questionnaire.csv (same fields as staff_facts), claims-signoff.json and the register's publish_rule. Those two claim stores will drift.
recommendation: Separate generated data from human-owned data. The questionnaire CSV holds staff facts and the G1/G2 sign-offs; the claims register gets signed_by and signed_on columns; drop claims-signoff.json. The merge never writes gate or staff fields, and the build joins the files.

scope: The Problem #5 (L25); §3 rows for general clinic pages and /physiotherapy-in-new-west/ (L133-134); D6 (L141); Alternative A (L261-265)
finding: research/07 §3.2, the source cited for Problem 5, says not to leave a second indexable WorkSafe location family. That means the legacy city pages and the 5 clinic pages with 'More About Worksafe' sections, including pilot Abbotsford. The draft only trims sentences on them and keeps /physiotherapy-in-new-west/ unchanged, so the pilot markets end up with several URLs for one intent and the pilot cannot attribute results. research/06 justified location pages as GBP landing pages because geo demand is zero, and D6 removes that half. Alternative A's rejection overreads the scope rule.
recommendation: Pick one WorkSafe owner URL per clinic, and cut the other pages' WorkSafe sections to one line plus a link in the same wave. Decide the New Westminster owner before the pilot. State the pilot hypothesis and the result that would retire the location-page layer.

scope: §4 gate table (L145-153); §6.2 uniqueness test (L217); Step 3.4 unique-text ratio (L328)
finding: G4 is hard-coded true for all clinics, so it gates nothing. G5 is a launch task tied to a paid tool with a noted subscription end, not a clinic property. Distinctness is defined three ways: a 4-of-7 field count, a review test and an untargeted text ratio. The review test as written fails every page, because it removes the unique bands and then judges the template remainder. G3 can pass on four short strings.
recommendation: Keep three gates: G1 contract, G2 NAP, G3 distinct facts. Move G4 and G5 to the runbook launch checklist. Define G3 once, either as the corrected test (keep only bands 2, 4, 5 and 6 with name and address stripped) or as the ratio with a threshold, and drop the other.

scope: §4 Scale rule (L163); §9 Cadence (L251); G-1 and G-2 (L31-32)
finding: Wave 2 starts after the day-30 review in §4, but the Wave 2/3 decision is at day 90 in §9. The day-30 criteria only show absence of harm; G-2 (day 60) and G-1 (day 90) carry the value. The program could grow from 3 to 17 location pages before any evidence they help.
recommendation: Use one decision point tied to value: day 60 with G-2 met in at least 2 of 3 pilot markets, or day 90 with G-1 and G-2. Wave 2 staff data collection can run in parallel.

finding: research/01 says existing schema is unknown and must be crawled before schema decisions. The site's duplicate canonicals and duplicate meta descriptions suggest two sources write the page head. The draft hand-declares Organization at a guessed @id, which risks a duplicate node, and adds a new #clinic entity per WorkSafe page, splitting one clinic into several entities.
recommendation: Run a Rich Results Test or view-source check of the live pillar and one clinic page first. Reuse the existing Organization @id. Give each clinic one canonical entity, on the general page, and have the WorkSafe page reference it by @id.

scope: §1 URL map (L99); Open Questions; claims register SYN-18
finding: WorkSafeBC provider-list pages rank #1 for wcb physio in Surrey, Abbotsford and New Westminster (research/08). Synergy's entries there are wrong or missing (SYN-18). The draft only links out to the lists and never plans the correction, which needs no build and the same ops contact as Q-1.
recommendation: Bundle a provider-list correction request with Q-1 (owner: ops/billing), and treat the provider list as a NAP surface under G2.

finding: The acceptance checklist says every page must pass, before publish, the rows 'GBP website links point to the matching page' and 'sameAs to GBP'. D6 keeps GBP on the general pages and §7 has no sameAs, so every location page fails the checklist by design, and the draft never reconciles the two.
recommendation: Amend the checklist row with the owner's sign-off, or drop D6. Either way, add sameAs (GBP URL where known) to the single clinic entity.

finding: The merge is Python with stdlib csv, while the build is to be no-dependency Node. That forces a hand-written CSV parser for the quote-heavy claims register that drives the claims gate (102 fields contain commas, 36 contain quotes) and a custom {{}} template language with conditionals. The repo already uses npm dependencies, so the constraint is self-imposed.
recommendation: Use one language: Python stdlib with plain functions returning strings, or Node with one CSV library. Write templates as plain functions; keep Playwright only for screenshots.

finding: Four custom GA4 events are defined before the existing taxonomy has been seen. GA4 enhanced measurement already logs outbound clicks to Jane, and CallTrackingMetrics already measures real calls.
recommendation: Start G-3 from outbound clicks filtered to janeapp.com plus CallTrackingMetrics calls per page. Add custom events only if those cannot separate placements.

finding: LCP and CLS are lab-tested on the fragment with a mock header, leaving out the 3+ MB of theme JavaScript that decides real speed, so the test always passes and tells nothing. The local screenshot matrix duplicates the WordPress draft preview at lower fidelity.
recommendation: Budget against the live page measured on the WordPress draft: 0 added JS, a capped CSS size, and no LCP or CLS regression. Keep one local preview for content review.

finding: Literal JSON shapes, CLI flags, four output files per page, QA field lists, rel handling and the em-dash lint are build-README material that buries the decisions. Separate schema.json and meta.json files also add manual paste steps.
recommendation: Move this detail to build/README or the runbook. Keep the inputs, the outputs (one fragment with embedded JSON-LD, plus title and meta) and the publish-mode refusal rules.

finding: §6.3 delivers the articles as drafts for the content owner, but Step 2.3 builds them as HTML fragments. That makes editorial posts hard-to-edit Custom HTML blocks inside the re-paste loop.
recommendation: Take the articles out of the build; deliver tagged copy to the content owner and check claims at review.

finding: The map is a directions link and the location page uses a nearby block, yet the CSS still ships the map iframe facade (.sr-ws-map) and the location selector (.sr-ws-locsel).
recommendation: Trim the CSS to the components §6.1 and §6.2 reference.

finding: Rule 1 says a title names only its owner cluster, but D3 keeps the pillar's head term in the coverage guide's title, against research/06 §7.2.
recommendation: Record D3 as a time-boxed exception, with a day-30 check of whether the guide and pillar alternate for the head term.

finding: The nearby-clinic regex runs across neighbouring entries and produces 16 rows over 15 clinics whose names are address fragments and whose slug is null. Band 7 would render them as they are, yet Step 1 is marked done.
recommendation: Fix the parser, or use coordinates or a staff-confirmed list. Add a build check that every nearby entry resolves to a known clinic slug.

finding: Band 3 shows dated collector data (WCB services and openings), while Future Improvements treats that same data source as not yet approved. The plugin README says live Jane collection stays off until Jane gives permission. Each refresh needs a collector and merge re-run.
recommendation: Use the collector output once as a seed, and make 'WCB services at this clinic' a staff-confirmed questionnaire field.

scope: §4 G3 (line 151); §6.2 uniqueness test (line 217); Step 3.4 (328); Step 4.2 (333); design-system.md §8.3
finding: G3 has three conflicting definitions: 4 of 7 facts filled (gate table); remove bands 2/4/5/6 and fail if the rest could describe any clinic (§6.2); and fill bands 2, 4, 5 (design-system, with different band numbers). After removing 2/4/5/6, what remains (hero, Jane services, nearby, sources/CTA) is all template-generated, so the test as written fails every page. The unique-text ratio has no formula or threshold. G3 is the only defence against the doorway risk in Problem 5.
recommendation: Give one G3 definition: which fields, how many, who verifies them. Restate the review test the intended way round (e.g. read only bands 2/4/5/6 with name and address removed; fail if they could describe another clinic). Define the unique-text metric and a pass threshold, and say whether this doc or design-system §8.3 numbering wins.

finding: Gates exist only for clinic pages, yet Q-1 blocks publishing 'any page'. The pillar's title, meta and '19+ clinics' tile assert SYN-01 (UNVERIFIED, per clinic). Band 3 tags billing 'SYN-07, SYN-08 pending G1' while §5 says Synergy statements carry SYN-01. The pillar has no clinic, so 'pending G1' has nothing to refer to (all 19 true? any? the sign-off?).
recommendation: Add a pillar publish rule (e.g. the pillar ships when ...; the finder and the '19+' count reflect only G1-true clinics). Pick one claim id for direct-billing and no-fee statements and say how it is checked on a page that belongs to no single clinic.

scope: G-4 (34); §5 (167); §6.1/§6.2 title and meta formulas; §7 availableService; Step 3.2 (326); Step 4.2 (333)
finding: §5 enforces claims via data-claim on elements, but titles, meta descriptions and JSON-LD cannot carry it. They still state WorkSafeBC or Synergy facts ('Bring your WorkSafeBC claim number', availableService 'WorkSafeBC physiotherapy', 'How claims, visits and costs work' while visit counts are barred). G-4 does not say whether these count. QA checks '19+ locations' wording but every title, meta and tile says '19+ clinics'. '19+' is not in the claims register. The em-dash rule has no stated reason.
recommendation: Add a rule for text outside elements (e.g. a claim-id list in meta.json checked by the build). Choose one '19+' wording and register it as a claim. Cite design-system E1 as the source of the em-dash and wording rules.

finding: §4 starts Wave 2 after the Wave 1 day-30 review. §9 puts the 'Wave 2/3 decision' at day 90. The reader cannot tell when Wave 2 starts.
recommendation: State one trigger for Wave 2 and one for Wave 3, and make §4 and §9 match.

finding: The 9 regional engines are never named. G-1's 'Baseline 0 of 9' reads as measured, but research/07 says no WorkSafe term is tracked and no baseline exists. The doc omits adding keywords at least 2 weeks before launch. Q-8 mentions the 2026-11-06 Data API expiry without saying it may stop the tracking that four goals depend on (research/07: unknown). G-6 names no AI engine (research/07 §7 I: ChatGPT 155491 only; AI Overview engines only in the ICBC project). '121 pairs' is not defined.
recommendation: Name the 9 engines. Mark the G-1 baseline as inferred and add 'tracking live at least 14 days before launch' to G5 or the timeline. State the consequence of the 2026-11-06 expiry and who renews. Name the AI engine(s) and list or link the 10 prompts. Define 'pair' as keyword x engine.

finding: G-3 reports events 'weekly from launch', but GA4 access does not exist and research/07 says it is unknown whether GA4 is configured. GA4/GTM readiness is not a prerequisite or gate. Only [data-sr-event] is named; the attributes carrying clinic_slug, placement and page_type, and the GTM variables and tags, are never specified. worksafe_location_select has no trigger. The per-100-sessions denominator needs GA4 sessions.
recommendation: List the data-sr-* attributes and their values, name the GTM variables and tags and who builds them, define the location_select trigger, and add verified GA4/GTM to the Wave 1 prerequisites.

finding: The doc never explains why contract status is unknown when every clinic offers WCB booking in Jane: the April 1, 2026 agreement did not carry existing clinics over (WSBC-01/03). It never says what 'contracted' changes for the worker (direct billing and no fees, versus paying and claiming back; WSBC-11/23/24/26). Wave 3 is justified only by the field name eligibility_risk; the reasons (absent from cached WorkSafeBC lists; Medimap shows Cedar Hills private-pay only, SYN-16) appear only in merge_locations.py. Q-2 does not say why Salius matters.
recommendation: Add a short 'Contract status' paragraph covering the 2026 agreement, what contracted means for the patient, and the per-clinic risk reasons (including Delta/Salius).

scope: Detailed Implementation Plan Steps 1.2-4 (314-333); §6.1/§6.2 title formulas; §7
finding: Only Step 1.1 is marked done, but build_pages.mjs, claims-signoff.json, pages/dist (20 pages) and qa-report.json already exist (commit 1b0caad), and they differ from the doc. Sources are pages/src/*.mjs, not .html templates with {{}} slots; there are extra --markers and --link flags; publish output goes to pages/publish/; built titles differ from the §6.1/§6.2 formulas; JSON-LD uses MedicalWebPage + WebSite; uniqueness is 5-word-shingle Jaccard. A reader cannot tell whether the doc is the spec or a stale description.
recommendation: Mark each step's status, describe the files that actually exist, and say which is authoritative when the doc and the build disagree.

scope: Step 1.1 (313); Step 1.3 (315); CUJ 4 (85-87); §6.2 band 7 (214); Future Improvements (305)
finding: 'Client-filled Yelp list', 'the collector's public data branch', 'the ICBC page data' and 'the existing availability widget' are undefined. They are actually yelp-nap.csv, availability.json on origin/data (from collect.js) and research/02-icbc-location-pages.csv. The script's required availability.json argument is unstated. merge_locations.py resets staff_facts to null and publish_gates to defaults on every run, so a refresh would erase the manual gate edits CUJ 4 tells Marketing to make. No step loads staff-questionnaire.csv into staff_facts.
recommendation: Name each source by path. Give the re-run command and its prerequisites. Make the merge keep gates and staff_facts, or forbid re-runs after manual edits. Add a step that imports the questionnaire.

finding: G4's condition ('§2 and §3 applied to the clinic') does not say what 'applied' means or who checks it, yet merge_locations.py sets G4 true for all 19 clinics. A gate that starts true does not gate anything.
recommendation: Give G4 a checklist (slug, title/H1 vs Rules 2-3, general clinic page edits per §3, other existing-URL dispositions), name who checks it, and default it to false.

finding: §6 hands band rhythm to design-system, but design-system §8.3 numbers the pillar 1-11 and the location page 1-9 with different contents from this doc's 12 and 8. design-system §9 gates on status VERIFIED, while §5 gates on publish_rule; they conflict (WSBC-13 PARTIAL/OK_TO_PUBLISH, WSBC-30 VERIFIED/STAFF_CONFIRM). modern-seo-cluster.md says every page 'must pass each row before publish', but this doc lists it only as a reference; it requires GBP links to the matching page (contradicts D6), sameAs to GBP (not in §7), INP under 200 ms (the NFR does not promise it) and a knowledge hub (deferred).
recommendation: State the precedence order among the three specs and reconcile band numbering, the claim criterion, and each conflicting modern-seo-cluster row (or mark those rows waived).

finding: The page is never described (a standalone landing template, possibly paid, never crawled, per research/01/09), even though it sits next to /physiotherapy-new-westminster/. The day-30 rule covers 'new page outranks' and 'alternate' but not 'the existing page stays ahead', which is exactly the case that fails G-2 in the strongest pilot market while §3 keeps it unchanged.
recommendation: Describe the page, add the missing day-30 branch, and say whether G-2 counts this page as success or failure.

finding: 'Allowed in drafts' could mean build preview output or WordPress drafts; if preview fragments go into WP drafts, a later re-paste is needed, and the doc does not say so. Loading worksafe.css only on WorkSafe URLs needs theme or plugin access, and nobody is named for it. The Elementor Full Width/Canvas layout design-system requires is not mentioned. Rollback ('set to draft, remove finder link') ignores that the finder is baked into the pillar fragment (rebuild and re-paste) and that sibling nearby blocks, general clinic pages and /physiotherapy-in-new-west/ also link to the page.
recommendation: Spell out each step from build mode to WordPress state, name who loads the CSS and how, and list every inbound link a rollback must remove, including the rebuild/re-paste steps.

finding: §5 asks staff to record a check date for each cited official URL, but the sign-off file has a single global checked_as_of and entries only for STAFF_CONFIRM rows. §5 also allows OK_TO_PUBLISH rows in publish mode with no condition, so it is unclear whether the official-page check blocks anything.
recommendation: Record checks per URL or per claim, and state that publish mode refuses any claim (including OK_TO_PUBLISH) whose official URL has no recorded check date.

scope: Goals G-1 to G-6 vs gates G1 to G5; §4 line 163; decisions D1-D6
finding: Goal ids (G-5) and gate ids (G5) nearly collide and appear in the same paragraph. D5 is missing between D4 and D6.
recommendation: Rename one series (e.g. goals O-1 to O-6) and renumber or explain the D5 gap.

finding: Undefined terms: Jane, SE Ranking and SE Ranking Local, ICBC (never expanded), GBP, Medimap, PHN, BC PIPA, _gl, Teleclaim, the KNOWN status value, 'Maps average 3.36' (a SE Ranking Local grid average), and the pillar's 'main line' (no number exists in the data).
recommendation: Add a short glossary and give the main-line phone number with its source.

finding: The doc says every number cites its file, but the Overview's own numbers (treatment 442; 8 of 78,145 impressions) are uncited, and the GSC figure drops research/07's caveats (date range and country unknown, top 1,000 rows only).
recommendation: Cite research/04 and research/07 and add the caveats.

finding: 'Hours today summary' needs today's date at view time, which a static fragment with no JavaScript cannot supply.
recommendation: Replace it with a static weekday/weekend summary or say how 'today' is computed.

finding: The specified pillar title is 68 characters, so the 65-character fallback always applies and the stated title never ships. 9 of the 19 location titles also exceed 65.
recommendation: State the title that actually ships.

finding: CUJ 3 promises links to each Surrey clinic's WorkSafe page, but no Surrey clinic is in Wave 1, so until Wave 2 the finder shows Jane links.
recommendation: Label CUJ 3 as the end state or describe what Wave 1 shows.

finding: The doc does not say where area_label comes from (ICBC page H1s via the merge script) or that some values are not neighbourhoods ('Surrey City Centre', 'King George Blvd, Surrey'), which matters for Rules 2 and 3.
recommendation: Name the source of area_label and list the 19 values.

scope: §2 near-me row (113) vs D6 (141); Non-Goals (43) vs §3 /icbc-claims/ (137); §2 Rule 4 (125); G-1/G-2 (31-32)
finding: Small contradictions: GBP listings are named as supporting URLs while D6 keeps GBP on the general clinic pages; the 'no ICBC changes' non-goal conflicts with the /icbc-claims/ edit; Rule 4 names no owner or action; G-2's 60 days have no start event; G-1 does not say whether both keywords must hit on the same engine.
recommendation: Fix each line.

finding: CallTrackingMetrics phone swapping (design-system E3, research/09 C-05) is missing from the list of inherited behaviours, although it changes visible phone numbers, tel: QA, NAP G2 and phone-click events.
recommendation: Add it and state how the NAP and event checks account for it.

finding: The gate is per page, but the contract fact belongs to the clinic. Every location page, including the three pilots after they pass all five gates, renders 'Book WCB physio at <neighbour>' Jane links, the FAQ line 'Our nearest clinics also book WCB physio online', and the nearest-WCB-massage sentence for ungated neighbours. All are tagged SYN-JANE (OK_TO_PUBLISH), so publish mode never blocks them. The build output shows New Westminster linking to Cedar Hills (HIGH risk, Wave 3), Abbotsford to Clayton Corners (HIGH risk) and Richmond to Delta (blocked by Q-2). The register itself says bookability is not proof of a contract. A pillar-level gate would not close this leak.
recommendation: Use one per-clinic WCB status (contract confirmed, with vendor number, who confirmed and when) that every mention reads: finder card, nearby card, FAQ sentence, CTA label and schema. An unconfirmed clinic never shows a WCB CTA or WCB claim anywhere. This replaces the G1 page gate and the SYN-01/SYN-08 special case in claim(). The pillar ships with clinic-independent facts only and a clinic count taken from confirmed clinics.

scope: Overview (L13), §2 rules 2-3 (L123-124), §4 waves (L155-163), §6.2, Steps 1-4; build_pages.mjs --link modes and cross-page Jaccard
finding: The architecture and tooling are sized for 19 pages. Measured WorkSafeBC physiotherapy demand is about 1,050 searches a month across Canada (BC share unknown), almost all in head terms the pillar owns, and geo demand is zero. Only 3 pilot pages can ship before the day-90 decision; none is in Surrey and none has a sibling within 2.5 km. So the close-sibling and Surrey rules, the 16 Wave 2/3 slugs, the nearby graph and the 19-page similarity checks govern pages that cannot exist within this document's horizon. The document never estimates the reachable WCB patient volume against other channels.
recommendation: Narrow the document to pillar + pilot + scaling criteria, and move the Wave 2/3 rules to a follow-up document informed by pilot data. If the pilot is meant to reduce scaling risk, include one close Surrey pair. Add a rough estimate of the prize: WCB patients from search vs provider lists, employers and Maps.

scope: Open Questions (L48-61), Non-Goals (L46), Detailed Implementation Plan Steps 1-5 (L309-338)
finding: The plan is all build steps, mostly already done in commit 1b0caad. Every launch blocker is outside the build: Q-1 (19 of 19 UNVERIFIED), WordPress access (not connected), GA4/GTM access (none), SE Ranking (Data API ends 2026-11-06, four days after the document date; unit balance inconsistent between ~9,300 and 1,320), and checks of worksafebc.com lines (blocked). None has a plan step, owner or date, and there is no outcome defined for Q-1 coming back 'some' or 'none'.
recommendation: Replace the Implementation Plan with a launch plan ordered by dependency. Step 0 covers Q-1 answers by a date, the SE Ranking renewal vs Search Console decision before 2026-11-06, and WordPress and GA4 access. Define the program shape for each Q-1 answer (all, some, none). Reduce the build steps to one line, and use the launch date as the start event for G-1 and G-2.

finding: The delivery model depends on page count and is not decided, so the hybrid carries the costs of both options. At pilot scale there is little to template, and the build only adds a paste step and a copy that will drift. At 19 pages, the site already loads Elementor Pro, JetEngine (post types, meta fields, listing grids), TeamPress (practitioner records by location) and Agile Store Locator, which together give one-field NAP edits, an automatic finder and nearby block, takedown by unpublishing one post, editing in fields, and server-rendered hours. The design builds a parallel CMS instead (JSON, Python merge, Node templates, claims engine, manual paste), and band 5 duplicates TeamPress.
recommendation: Add an Alternatives entry, 'WordPress-native rendering (JetEngine and Theme Builder) vs static fragments', decided by page count. For the pilot, author directly in WordPress. At scale, use a clinic post type with one single template and a listing-grid finder, with gates as post status plus required fields. Reuse TeamPress for the WCB team band. Confirm plugin licences once WordPress access exists.

scope: Overview (L11), §6.2 band 3 (L210), band 6 (L213), Step 1.1 (L313); build/merge_locations.py; collect.js; plugin README in the zip
finding: Page content depends on availability.json from collect.js, a headless-browser collector that calls Jane's openings API around the clock. The repo's own Synergy Next Availability README says Jane's Acceptable Use Policy prohibits bot collection and that live collection stays off until Jane gives written permission. The design uses this feed for WCB service types, massage answers, counts of physios with openings and the dated 'as of' line. SYN-JANE says to re-check before every publish, which makes re-running the merge routine, and that re-run is what wipes gate state.
recommendation: Take the collector out of the page data flow. Get WCB appointment types per clinic once from the clinic questionnaire or a Jane admin export, and drop the counts of openings this week. This removes the compliance exposure, the dated-data problem and the reason to re-run the merge.

scope: §5 (L165-173), G-4 (L34), Step 3.2 (L326), NFR rollback (L292), §3 existing-page rows (L132-139)
finding: Fact control runs only on the fragment before paste. After paste, WordPress is the source of truth and nothing re-checks it, whether editors change copy, WorkSafeBC changes rules, a contract lapses, or wrong facts stay live on the homepage, /icbc-claims/ and ICBC clinic pages. Extending the build to cover titles, meta and JSON-LD adds machinery at a layer that still cannot see drift.
recommendation: Add a recurring audit of the rendered live pages, reusing the repo's scheduled GitHub Actions pattern. It should flag register DO_NOT_PUBLISH phrasings, WCB CTAs to clinics without a confirmed contract, and stale 'as of' dates, with a named owner and a cadence (monthly and on WorkSafeBC changes). Treat data-claim tags as an authoring aid and a pre-publish review checklist rather than the main control.

finding: The measurement plan (about 121 SE Ranking pairs on a subscription with an unknown future, 10 AI prompts, 4 custom GA4 events via GTM on a site with three GA4 gtags and two Meta pixels and no GA4 access, ±3 guardrails) is heavier than the two decisions it serves: scale or not, and keep, narrow or noindex per page. None of it counts WCB bookings.
recommendation: Make the primary measures Search Console at page level (free, direct) and Jane appointment reports of WCB Physio Initial bookings per clinic per week, comparing pilot with non-pilot clinics over a 4 to 8 week pre-launch baseline. Keep SE Ranking and the GA4 events as optional extras once access exists, consistent with the no-paid-tools non-goal.

finding: The design adds a second design system for a handful of pages: a 59 KB stylesheet with 162 sr-ws- classes, its own tokens, radii and shadows, a new body font (Inter, which the site likely does not load), and a 753-line design-system spec, all inside an existing Elementor kit. Kit changes will not reach these pages, editors cannot extend them with native widgets, the CSS needs conditional enqueue (theme access with no owner), and it forces hand-coded HTML.
recommendation: Use the Elementor kit globals and native widgets (accordion, icon list, buttons). Keep a small scoped stylesheet only for components the kit lacks, such as steps and finder cards, and drop the extra font family.

scope: §6 (L177), Additional Resources (L296-300); design-system.md, modern-seo-cluster.md, PROJECT-STATE.md, build/ and pages/src/
finding: The conflicts the earlier stages found across documents and code (band numbers, VERIFIED vs publish_rule, 'must pass' checklist rows, build output that differs from the spec) share one cause: no artifact is declared the one that wins.
recommendation: Declare design_draft.md normative and mark the other documents as informative, or fold the needed rules into it. State whether code follows the document or the reverse.

finding: The pillar has no publish gate. Gates G1-G5 apply only to location pages, yet the pillar's title, meta, hero, trust tiles ('19+ clinics', 'WCB online booking') and finder ('Book WCB assessment' Jane link for all 19, including HIGH-risk Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners) all assert WorkSafeBC physio at every clinic while SYN-01 is UNVERIFIED for all 19. The per-clinic SYN-01/SYN-08 coupling never fires for pillar statements, so one global SYN-08 sign-off unblocks 'we bill WorkSafeBC' everywhere. Title and meta cannot carry data-claim and bypass §5 entirely. '19+' is not in the claims register. Harm: a worker books WCB at a clinic not contracted under the April 2026 agreement and pays out of pocket, reimbursed only at $95/visit (WSBC-26).
recommendation: Define a pillar gate. The finder offers WCB booking only for clinics with G1 true. Title, meta and tile counts are computed from G1-true clinics, without '+'. Pillar-level Synergy statements require G1 for every clinic they imply. Title, meta and JSON-LD go through the same claim check as body copy.

scope: Whole document (risk content scattered across lines 25, 163, 257, 289-292)
finding: There is no Risks & Mitigations section, which the standard requires. Unaddressed failure modes: a clinic's contract lapses after its page is live (no takedown SLA or owner); WorkSafeBC changes rules (PABC expects a new agreement, WSBC-09) with no re-check cadence; rank tracking stops when SE Ranking's API expires 2026-11-06; a merge-script re-run wipes gate state; static fragments drift from the repo; health-adjacent analytics reaches ad tools.

scope: design_draft.md lines 110-115, 122-124, 181, 202-203 (§2 rules 1 and 3; §6.1 and §6.2 titles and H1s)
finding: Head-term ownership is inverted by the doc's own formulas. recommendation: Location titles and H1s lead with neighbourhood and street, without the bare head term. Keep both 'WorkSafeBC' and 'WCB' in the pillar title within 65 characters. Add a Surrey H2 in the finder. Declare the spec normative and lint titles against the owner table in the build.

finding: The coverage guide keeps 'WorkSafeBC physiotherapy' in its title. That breaks rule 1 and goes against research/06 §7.2 and research/01, which rate the guide a High cannibalization risk. CUJ2 routes the pending-claim query to a full pillar FAQ answer, although §2 assigns pending claims to the guide. Pillar bands 2, 4 and 10 duplicate the guide's measured-question H2s. research/07 (0 ranking keywords) and research/08 (ranks in 4 cities) disagree, and the doc does not reconcile them.
recommendation: Choose one owner per question: the pillar gives 1-2 sentences plus a link, or the guide is merged into the pillar with a 301. Align CUJ2. If the guide keeps the head term, document the trade-off and add a pillar-vs-guide alternation alarm.

finding: '94% shared text causes ~5 URLs per query to rotate' and '17 of 29 rank the wrong clinic's page' are causal claims the data does not support. The 5.0 distinct URLs span every ICBC URL family (hub, /icbc-physiotherapy-in-*, blogs). The ICBC location pages first ranked on 2026-10-02, so the 31-day window is post-indexing settling. research/07 says 'a different page', not always the wrong clinic. The mitigation (own area label in the H1) is what the ICBC pages already have: area_label is copied from the ICBC H1 in merge_locations.py.
recommendation: Restate the claim as a correlation. Separate cross-family churn from sibling churn and re-measure ICBC after 60-90 days. Base the mitigation on measures the ICBC pages lack: a similarity threshold, removal of the second WorkSafe URL family, and substantive unique facts.

finding: The uniqueness test is inverted. Removing the unique bands 2, 4, 5 and 6 leaves the shared template, which always 'could describe any other clinic', so every page fails or the test is ignored. G3's '4 of 7' can be met with low-information facts ('nearby workplaces served' is a marketing claim). The build reports 5-shingle Jaccard similarity of 0.42-0.53 with no threshold, and never compares a page with the same clinic's ICBC page, which already ranks for WorkSafe queries in Richmond and Abbotsford.
recommendation: Use a swap test: put another clinic's name and NAP on the page; if every sentence is still true, fail. Set a numeric maximum similarity (for example 0.35) against siblings and the same clinic's /icbc-treatments/ page, enforced in publish mode. Define minimum specificity per G3 fact.

scope: design_draft.md lines 155-163, 125 (§4 waves and scale rule)
finding: Wave 1 is three single-clinic markets: no Surrey clinic, no close pair. The cannibalization gate is unlikely to fire there. Wave 2 then publishes 14 pages at once, including 9 Surrey clinics and the King George/Newton pair (2.4 km), which are exactly the conditions behind the ICBC churn.
recommendation: Add one Surrey close pair or cluster to Wave 1, or split Wave 2 into Surrey sub-waves with their own day-30 review. Give numeric pass criteria: maximum distinct WorkSafe URLs per query per engine, and minimum pillar share for Surrey queries.

finding: §3 only swaps visit-count and fee sentences. Left untouched: the 5 newer clinic pages with full WorkSafe sections (including /physiotherapy-abbotsford-chiropractor/ in the Abbotsford pilot), 66 legacy pages saying 'We Accept ICBC, WCB, MSP', /richmond-physiotherapy-2/ (#7 for wcb physio richmond, Richmond pilot), the shared Clayton page, neighbourhood pages and 35 /extp-location/ archives. research/07 §3.2 warns against leaving a second indexable WorkSafe location family.

finding: /physiotherapy-in-new-west/ stays unchanged at #3/#3/#6 and remains an AI Overview source, while G-2 requires the new New Westminster page to be the best-ranking Synergy URL within 60 days. finding: A ±3 tolerance against a single-day baseline is far narrower than observed volatility. 30-day ranges: icbc physiotherapy Delta 1-80, Richmond 1-79, Vancouver 1-56; icbc physio New Westminster 2-72; car accident physiotherapy Abbotsford baseline #85 (data/rank-baseline.csv). The guardrail will false-alarm and cannot attribute changes to WorkSafe pages.
recommendation: Use research/07 §7E's URL-takeover rule (alarm when a guardrail term's ranking URL becomes a WorkSafe page), plus a rolling 28-day median comparison with per-pair tolerance.

finding: Measurement depends on access that is not secured. The SE Ranking Data API expires 2026-11-06 and continued rank tracking is UNKNOWN. finding: merge_locations.py rewrites the whole worksafe-locations.json with gates false and staff_facts null, and CUJ4 has Marketing hand-edit the same file, so a re-run wipes gate and staff-fact state. finding: The build validates only elements already tagged with data-claim. Untagged facts, titles, meta descriptions and JSON-LD pass unchecked, so G-4 cannot be enforced. recommendation: Allow multiple claim ids per element. Validate title, meta and JSON-LD. Add a lint for WorkSafeBC terms or numbers outside tagged elements, plus a named reviewer step. Align design-system §13 and §15 with publish_rule.

scope: design_draft.md lines 34, 171, 195, 210, 48-61 (G-4; §5 visit-count rule; band 9; location band 3; Open Questions)

scope: design_draft.md lines 119, 195, 210 (WCB massage and acupuncture sections)

finding: Hand-pasted static fragments mean any data change (Jane types, hours, 'as of' date, a sibling going live) requires a rebuild and re-paste across many pages, with no drift detection. finding: Alternative A's rejection is circular: the scope rule governs the new pages themselves, and A's main advantages are not weighed. scope: design_draft.md lines 67-69, 189, 204 (CUJ1; steps band; location meta)

scope: design_draft.md lines 141, 177, 196, 226-229, 290 (D6; §6; §7; NFR performance) vs spec/modern-seo-cluster.md

finding: G3 treats the consented clinic photo as optional (4 of 7), but publish mode blocks on a missing hero photo, which makes it mandatory in practice.

scope: Whole document; missing H2 between Alternatives Considered (L259) and Non-Functional Requirements (L287)

scope: §1 D3 (L104) vs §2 rule 1 (L122) and owner table (L111, L117)

scope: Goals L31-36; gates table L147-153; usages L52, L56-59, L136, L157, L163, L173, L189; decision IDs L102-105, L141
finding: Goal IDs (G-1..G-6) and gate IDs (G1..G5) differ only by a hyphen, and lines such as L163 'no G-5 regressions' and L173/L189 'G1' depend on the reader noticing it. Decision IDs jump from D4 to D6. D5 is missing, which suggests a deleted decision.

finding: The intro says each question blocks only the items named, but Q-9 and Q-10 name nothing. finding: Publish gates are defined only for clinic pages. The pillar, coverage guide and RTW article have no publish criteria, yet Q-1 'blocks publishing any page'. The pillar title, meta and trust tile ('19+ Clinics') and band 3 billing statement assert SYN-01 (STAFF_CONFIRM, UNVERIFIED) for all clinics, including HIGH-risk Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners. finding: §5 says direct-billing elements carry data-claim='SYN-01', but §6.1 band 3 tags the same statement SYN-08 'pending G1'. Status is annotated three ways ('pending G1', 'pending', nothing). The band 2 referral answer depends on WSBC-16 (STAFF_CONFIRM, blocked by Q-4) and is not marked. Build refusal is keyed to these tags.

scope: §2 rule 2 L123 vs §6.2 title L202; §6.1 title L181
finding: Rule 2 requires each page title to use its own area label and street. scope: §6.2 band 1 L208 vs §10 L256 and NFR L290

scope: §3 table L129-139; gate G4 L152; build/merge_locations.py L93-94
finding: The existing-URL decision table omits URLs flagged in research/09 §3.1: /richmond-physiotherapy-2/ (#7 in pilot Richmond, which bears on G-2), /physiotherapy-delta-chiropractor/ (Delta GBP landing, organic #2) and Newton's GBP target /physiotherapy-amson-chiropractor/. finding: Nearby clinics come from the ICBC data, but in data/worksafe-locations.json 16 nearby entries across 15 of 19 clinics (including pilots Richmond and Abbotsford) have slug null and garbled names. §7 sets hasMap 'where the GBP maps URL is KNOWN', but the data has no maps-URL field at all. scope: Additional Resources L299 vs §4, §6.1 band 10 L196, §7 L226-228, NFR L290
finding: spec/modern-seo-cluster.md says every pillar and location page must pass each row before publish. finding: Rollback is defined only for location pages and the pillar. finding: The document says 'Every number below cites its file' but leaves several figures uncited (subscription end date, 9 massage clinics, distances, #3/#4 and Maps 3.36, 9 in-links, about 8 KB), and the Overview numbers are uncited. research/04 supplies the Wave 1 Maps data but is never cited, and it contradicts L158: Abbotsford tracks no WorkSafe Maps keyword, so Maps effects there cannot be measured as stated. research/09 (source of the gates and open questions) is never cited.

finding: Both are H3 directly under the H2 'Non-Functional Requirements', so the outline nests them as NFR subsections.

finding: D1 and Alt B claim both head terms 'show a local pack (research/06)'. research/06 lists local_pack only for 'wcb physiotherapy'; 'worksafebc physiotherapy' SERP features are 'Not Available'. research/08 live SERP for 'worksafebc physiotherapy' (Vancouver, task 264768352) shows Local pack: none. research/06 finding 3 also says part of the 210/mo 'wcb physiotherapy' volume is out of province. recommendation: Rewrite: "`wcb physiotherapy` (210/mo Canada-wide, partly out of province) shows a local pack (research/06). `worksafebc physiotherapy` (140/mo) showed no local pack in the 2026-11-02 Vancouver SERP (research/08)." Re-derive the D1 and Alt B rationale from this.

finding: 'Every number below cites its file' is false. Uncited numbers: 8 of 78,145 impressions and treatment 442 (line 11), 2026-11-06 (59), 9 massage clinics (119), clinic distances (123), #3/#4 and Maps 3.36 (156), 9 in-links (270), 8 KB (290). finding: The baselines are presented as measured. research/07 states 'There is no rank-tracking baseline for WorkSafe today' and 'there is no AI-visibility baseline for WorkSafe'. finding: The goals are imprecise. G-1 does not say whether both keywords or only one must rank per engine. G-2 'within 60 days' has no start event. finding: Goal IDs G-1 to G-6 and gate IDs G1 to G5 differ only by a hyphen. 'G2' is the NAP gate and 'G-2' is the Right-page goal. Cross-references such as 'G-5 guardrails', 'fails G3' and 'if G1 is false' are easy to misread.

finding: (a) 'Launch Rehab ... ranks #1 in New Westminster': research/08 shows the #1 result is Launch's Coquitlam clinic page, which weakens the per-clinic argument. finding: The causal claim 'cause Google to rotate about 5 Synergy URLs per query' is not shown by the data. research/07 reports a 31-day average of 5.0 distinct URLs per keyword-engine pair (not per query), across two URL families: /icbc-treatments/ (36 of 93 ranking pairs) and the older /icbc-physiotherapy-in-{x}/ (27 of 93).

finding: Predictions are stated as facts: 'so it does not drop its current rankings', 'New WorkSafe pages displace them for WorkSafe queries by relevance', 'would pull generic physio near me demand onto WorkSafe-only pages'.
recommendation: State each as an expected outcome with a check: 'intended to preserve its rankings; checked at day 30 against research/08 positions'; 'expected to outrank them for WorkSafe queries; monitored under §2 rule 4'.

finding: Subjective words carry decision rationale: 'strongest existing WorkSafe signal' and 'the SERPs are weak' justify the pilot markets (research/08 labels 'weak' LIKELY). Others: 'win', 'main risk', 'genuinely distinct', 'dead CrazyEgg/Contentsquare scripts'.

Drop 'genuinely'.

finding: 'All register rows were verified from search snippets' contradicts the next sentence (staff must open each URL) and research/05 §0 (snippet quotes, pages not opened). finding: 'Pending' means both a WorkSafeBC claim status (pending claim, pending vs accepted) and a sign-off status ('WSBC-49 pending', 'WSBC-36 pending', 'SYN-07, SYN-08 pending G1'). The band 4 cell uses both meanings. SYN-07 is OK_TO_PUBLISH, so 'pending' is wrong for it.
recommendation: Use 'pending' only for claim status. Mark sign-off state with the register value (STAFF_CONFIRM) or 'awaiting sign-off'. Remove the label from SYN-07.

finding: 'Owner' has four meanings: the business owner (scope rule, 'Owner decision'), the keyword target URL ('Owner URL', 'designated owner of Surrey city queries'), the responsible team (gate table), and the content owner (line 221).
recommendation: Use 'business owner (<role>)', 'target URL', 'responsible team' and 'content editor' consistently, and add them to a short glossary.

finding: §5 says Synergy-specific statements carry data-claim="SYN-01". Band 3 tags the billing sentence with SYN-07 and SYN-08 instead. SYN-07 covers reporting and the claim number, not billing. The build's publish refusal depends on these tags.
recommendation: Define one rule, e.g., 'Billing and no-fee sentences carry SYN-08; the build also requires gate G1 (SYN-01) for that clinic.' Specify the syntax for multiple claim ids per element.

finding: Rule 1 says title, H1 and first paragraph name only the owner cluster. D3 keeps 'WorkSafeBC physiotherapy' (the pillar cluster) in the coverage guide title, and the location title includes 'WCB Physiotherapy' (also the pillar cluster). The rule cannot be met as written.
recommendation: Restate rule 1 in measurable terms (e.g., 'the first keyword in the title and the H1 is the page's owner cluster; pillar terms may appear only after the separator') or change the conflicting titles.

finding: The pillar title is 68 characters, over the 65 limit, so the 55-character fallback always ships. The location template gives 69 to 70 characters for New Westminster, Strawberry Hill, Sullivan Heights and Clayton Corners; of the names tested, only Vancouver (63) fits. The spec presents the exception as the primary title and does not say what happens if a title is still over 65 after shortening.
recommendation: Specify the shipped titles ('WorkSafeBC Physiotherapy at 19+ Locations | Synergy Rehab' or similar) and the behaviour when the shortened title still exceeds 65 characters.

finding: Not compliant with the cited copy standard (design-system §13): 'Use 19+ locations exactly', but the draft uses '19+ Clinics', '19+ Synergy Rehab clinics' and '19+ clinics', and line 11 says '19 clinics'. The CUJ 1 CTA 'Book a WCB initial assessment' is 29 characters (limit 28) and has no clinic name, which location pages require. The trust tile 'evening and weekend hours' has no claim id, and Clayton Corners has no Saturday or Sunday hours in worksafe-locations.json.
recommendation: Use '19+ locations' everywhere. Change the CTA to a label of 28 characters or fewer that includes the clinic, e.g., 'Book WCB physio at New West'. Tag each trust tile with a claim id or remove it, and qualify the hours claim.

finding: Conflicts with the cited specs: FAQ answers 40 to 80 words here vs 40 to 60 in modern-seo-cluster; hero image under 120 KB WebP here vs 150 KB AVIF or WebP in design-system §11; INP 'reported, not promised' vs INP under 200 ms; D6 keeps GBP links on general pages vs 'GBP website links point to the matching page'; §5 gates on publish_rule vs design-system §13 'maps to a VERIFIED claim_id'.
recommendation: State which document takes precedence, then align the numbers and rules, or list each deliberate deviation with a reason.

finding: 'Every required clinic-fact slot is filled' (CUJ 4) conflicts with G3 'at least 4 of these' 7 facts. The set of 'required' slots is never defined, yet the build is meant to stop on empty required slots.
recommendation: List the required slots explicitly (e.g., name, street, phone, hours, Jane URL, plus any 4 of the 7 staff facts) and use the same list in CUJ 4, G3 and the build.

finding: The test cannot be measured and its logic is unclear. After removing bands 2, 4, 5 and 6, the hero still carries the clinic's name, street and phone, so 'could describe any other clinic' never applies, or always applies, depending on how it is read. There is no threshold.
recommendation: Define a numeric test, e.g., 'With clinic name, address, phone and hours masked, unique-text ratio vs every other location page >= X% (qa-report.json)'. Name which elements are masked.

finding: The start of Wave 2 is stated three ways: after the day-30 review (line 163), at the 'day 90 goal review and Wave 2/3 decision' (line 251), and as a '30-day pilot review' (line 283).
recommendation: State one decision point for Wave 2 and one for Wave 3, each with its pass criteria, and reference it from all three places.

finding: The 'Reason for Rejection' entries for B, C and D restate the selected design instead of saying why the alternative fails. A uses the vague 'The evidence favours'. The Pros 'Mirrors some competitors' and 'Fastest coverage' are vague. 'Doorway risk' is undefined.
recommendation: Give each rejection a falsifiable reason tied to a cited fact (e.g., B: 'informational page cannot carry 19 clinic cards without diluting its claim-question intent'). Name competitors and quantify 'fastest'. Define doorway pages with a reference.

finding: Undefined terms: NAP, GBP, SERP, GA4, GTM, PHN, BC PIPA, LCP/CLS/INP, Jane, the label 'KNOWN', 'P2', and 'Elephant' in the byline. RTW is used at line 98 and defined only at line 105.

finding: Decision numbering skips D5 (D1 to D4, then D6).
recommendation: Renumber or note that D5 was removed.

finding: Mixed shorthand for the program: 'WorkSafe', 'Worksafe', 'WorkSafeBC', 'WCB' and 'WSBC'. Line 11 defines only WCB.
recommendation: Add one rule: 'WorkSafe' = project and page-family label; 'WorkSafeBC' in factual statements; 'WCB' only in keywords and Jane treatment names.

finding: Vague phrases: 'search presence'; 'within the first screen' and 'within one scroll' (no viewport); '(via local relevance)'; 'the owner table above decides' (the table specifies no actions); '(kept short)'; 'baseline before launch' (research/07 asks for at least 2 weeks).
recommendation: Replace with measurable wording, e.g., 'above the fold at 390x844', 'baseline collected for at least 14 days before launch', 'shared content <= N words per band'.

finding: Noise or out-of-scope text: a rel="noopener" rule for a case marked 'not used'; 'Separate recommendation outside this project'; 'must be fixed site-wide' with no owner; the subscription end date with no consequence; 'Proposed solution in one line' for a multi-clause sentence.
recommendation: Delete the noopener clause and the out-of-scope recommendation (move it to REPORT.md). Assign or remove 'must be fixed site-wide'. Add the consequence of the 2026-11-06 expiry (rank tracking continuity UNKNOWN, research/07). Rename the label to 'Proposed solution'.

finding: New Westminster rankings appear as '#3, #3, #6' (line 133) and '#3/#4' (line 156). The #4 belongs to the coverage guide (research/08), not a New Westminster page.
recommendation: Use one format with URLs and keywords, e.g., '/physiotherapy-in-new-west/ #3 (worksafebc), #3 (wcb physio), #6 (workplace injury); coverage guide #4 (worksafebc)'.

finding: 'Google Search Central guidance on doorway pages and scaled content' has no URL or date. 'The existing availability widget' has no reference.
recommendation: Add the URLs with access dates, and cite design-system §2 for the widget.

finding: The pillar tells users WorkSafeBC care is available at all 19 clinics and links them to book at clinics whose contract is unverified. Title 'WorkSafeBC Physiotherapy at 19+ Clinics' (design_draft.md:181). Meta 'Book a WCB physiotherapy assessment at one of 19+ Synergy Rehab clinics' (:183). Band 8 gives every unpublished clinic a 'Book WCB assessment' Jane link (:194). As built: pillar.mjs:76 'see a contracted physiotherapist... Book... at any of our 19+ locations'; :205 'WCB physiotherapy at 19+ locations'; :121 SYN-08 'We bill WorkSafeBC' has no clinic attached, so one global sign-off unlocks it. The gates in §4 apply only to location pages, so nothing gates the pillar. SYN-01 is UNVERIFIED for all 19 clinics. Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners are on no cached WorkSafeBC physio list (research/05 §6). A worker who books a non-contracted clinic pays and is reimbursed only at WorkSafeBC's rate (WSBC-26).
recommendation: Add a pillar gate. Every WorkSafeBC or billing statement and every WCB CTA on the pillar must be scoped to clinics with G1 true. Use a title without a count, e.g. 'WorkSafeBC (WCB) Physiotherapy | Synergy Rehab', or a count the build derives from G1-true clinics. In the finder, clinics with G1 false get no WCB booking link; show 'WorkSafeBC status being confirmed, call the clinic' or leave them out. Add a publish-mode build check that fails if any page carries a Jane WCB URL or SYN-08/SYN-09 text for a clinic with G1 false.

scope: §6.2 bands 6 and 7 (nearby clinics, 'nearest clinic if this one is full' FAQ); §8 nearby links
finding: Published Wave 1 pages send WorkSafe patients to unverified clinics. Nearby cards link to the other clinic's Jane WCB booking when it has no WorkSafe page (location.mjs:66-68). The FAQ 'Our nearest clinics also book WCB physio online: ...' (location.mjs:45) is tagged SYN-JANE, which is OK_TO_PUBLISH, so it passes publish mode. New Westminster (Wave 1) lists Cedar Hills (5.9 km, eligibility_risk HIGH, not on any cached WorkSafeBC physio list) and Central City as its nearest options.
recommendation: Filter the nearby block and the nearest-clinic FAQ to clinics with G1 true. If none is within a sensible distance, link to the pillar finder instead. Change §6.2 band 7 to: 'links only to clinics whose G1 is true; other clinics are not shown'. Enforce it with the same build check as the pillar fix.

scope: Detailed Implementation Plan, Step 3.3 / Step 5; NFR Rollout
finding: Step 3.3 (design_draft.md:327) says to paste `pages/dist/<page>/fragment.html` into WordPress. `pages/dist` is the preview build; publish mode writes to `pages/publish/` (build_pages.mjs:18). All 19 dist fragments carry the hero pill 'WorkSafeBC contracted' and 'We bill WorkSafeBC directly', including Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners (e.g. dist/cedar-hills-surrey/fragment.html: `<span data-claim="SYN-01" data-claim-status="pending" ...>WorkSafeBC contracted`). The dashed pending and staff-slot styles exist only in the preview CSS. worksafe.css has none, so a pasted draft shows the contract claim with nothing marking it as unverified, plus raw 'Staff to confirm' text.
recommendation: Correct Step 3.3 and the runbook: only `pages/publish/<page>/fragment.html` may be pasted. In preview mode, either stop writing fragment.html, or render SYN-01/SYN-08 as 'Contract status: staff to confirm' instead of the claim and put a visible 'PREVIEW, DO NOT PUBLISH' banner inside the fragment itself. Add a RUNBOOK check: grep the WordPress draft for data-claim-status before publishing.

scope: §6.2 uniqueness test; Step 3.4 / Step 4.2 unique-text ratio
finding: The uniqueness test is inverted and has no measurable threshold. 'Remove bands 2, 4, 5 and 6. If what remains could describe any other clinic, the page fails G3' (design_draft.md:217). Bands 2, 4, 5 and 6 are the only clinic-specific bands. What remains (hero NAP, band 3 service flags, nearby links, sources and CTA) is template, so by construction it always describes any other clinic. Every page then fails, or reviewers count NAP as distinct and every page passes. The only number available, the build's 'unique-text ratio', is raw 5-gram Jaccard (build_pages.mjs:143-145, 219-222). It reads 0.418 to 0.530 (qa-report.json) because the clinic name appears in nearly every sentence. With names, area labels, addresses, phones, times and numbers normalised, the pages are 0.81 to 1.00 similar. Five pages are identical to a sibling (Cedar Hills, Central City, Clayton Heights, Langley, Sullivan Heights), and the median page shares 99% of its 5-grams with its closest sibling. That is worse than the ICBC set's about 94% shared copy (research/02:162). No owner, record or build check exists for the test.
recommendation: Rewrite the test. Remove bands 1, 3, 7 and 8 and all template-generated sentences. What remains must be at least about 200 words of verified clinic-only facts and must answer at least 3 worker questions that the pillar finder card cannot. In the build, normalise clinic and NAP tokens before shingling. Fail publish mode if max normalised Jaccard against any other published WorkSafe page, or against the same clinic's ICBC page, exceeds an agreed ceiling (e.g. 0.70), or if clinic-only words fall below the floor. Store the reviewer's pass in worksafe-locations.json (G3_review: {by, date}) and have the build require it.

finding: G3 counts fields; it does not test whether a page is distinct. The pass condition is any 4 of 7 fields non-empty (design_draft.md:151; build_pages.mjs:41, 210-211), with no minimum length and no verification record. Two of the seven never render: `nearby_workplaces` appears in no template, and the template takes photos from data/photos.json, which has no consent field, not from `photo_with_consent`. `check_in` renders (location.mjs:149) but is not counted. Parking from Yelp is the same template value on all 19 rows (research/09 A-03). The draft drops research/09 §2.2's requirement that bands 2, 4 and 5 be filled, including a consented WCB team and a consented photo. A clinic can pass G3 with about four short strings and publish a name-swapped template with roughly 100 unique words, about the same amount that varies between ICBC pages.
recommendation: Redefine G3 over rendered fields only. Required: getting_here, accessibility, check_in and parking, each manager-verified, not taken from Yelp, and at least about 25 words. Also required: languages, plus at least one of a consented team card or a consented clinic photo. Track the photo's consent in photos.json and let the build count only fields that actually render. Remove nearby_workplaces from G3 (see the separate finding). Create data/staff-questionnaire.csv with these exact fields.

finding: Nearby-clinic data is corrupt for 15 of 19 clinics. In merge_locations.py km_list, the regex `0\d (.+?) About` also matches inside street numbers: '8045 204 Street' yields a clinic named 'Street, Unit A130, Langley Twp ; 02 Clayton Heights', with slug None. Five pages render garbled FAQ text. One is Wave 1 Abbotsford ('Langley (about 24 km) and Street, Unit A130, Langley Twp ; 02 Clayton Heights'). Newton's FAQ prints King George's address next to Sullivan Heights ('8056 King George Blvd, Surrey ; 02 Sullivan Heights'). Unresolved entries silently drop their card (location.mjs:65 `if (!t) return ''`), so real neighbours vanish, e.g. Nordel loses Central City at 3.0 km. No QA step in Step 4.2 would catch this.
recommendation: Parse the component by splitting on ' ; ' and matching `^(\d{2}) (.+?) About ([\d.]+) km` per entry. Make the build fail if any nearby name does not resolve to a known clinic slug. Recompute distances from geocoded addresses, and state on the page whether they are road or straight-line distances (research/09 A-09: method UNKNOWN). Add 'every nearby entry resolves' to the Step 4.2 QA list.

finding: The template data the document labels 'unique' is mostly shared. The hours FAQ answer is the same sentence ('Yes. We are open 7 days a week, and our latest closing time is 8:30 PM') on 15 to 16 of 19 pages (worksafe-locations.json hours). Band 3 has only three variants: physio only (10 clinics), physio plus massage (8), physio plus massage plus acupuncture (Nordel). Band 7 is navigation. Apart from staff facts, nothing on the page is information the pillar finder card or Jane does not already give.
recommendation: Relabel these bands as shared and stop counting them toward uniqueness. Replace the hours and massage FAQ items with clinic-only questions the manager answers: which entrance or floor; whether there is elevator or step-free access; how long a first WCB visit takes here; whether a forms or claim-number desk exists; which transit lines stop nearby. Keep hours in the hours table.

finding: The close-clinic rules are not sound. (a) They set naming only. Nothing decides whether both clinics in a close pair get pages; research/09 A-09 and B-05 asked for exactly that decision. (b) 'Clayton' is in both Clayton clinics' names, so rule 2 cannot be satisfied. ICBC already alternates them for 'clayton physiotherapy' (research/07 §2.4: target clayton-heights, ranking clayton-corners, 2 URLs), and the legacy /clayton-physiotherapy-treatment-clinic/ covers both (research/09 A-11). (c) Rule 2 handles pairs under 2.5 km, but Surrey is a cluster: Nordel, Cedar Hills, Central City, King George, Newton and Strawberry Hill all sit within about 3.5 km (Nordel to King George 2.8, Nordel to Central City 3.0, King George to Strawberry Hill 3.0). (d) The distances come from the ICBC component, whose measurement method is UNKNOWN, and 16 clinics have no coordinates. (e) There are name collisions: WorkSafeBC lists Central City as 'Synergy Rehabilitation King George Hub' (SYN-18) while another clinic is named King George, and the site taxonomy files Nordel as 'Nordel (North Delta)' while the Delta page's H1 is 'North Delta'. (f) Rule 2 requires the street in the title and H1, but the §6.2 formulas contain no street.
recommendation: Add a cluster rule. Within any group of clinics under about 3.5 km apart, publish one at a time, and the second page must exceed the first's normalised-distinctness bar. Name an owner for shared tokens (bare 'Clayton' goes to the pillar Surrey group or one designated page). Add the street to the title or H1 formula as rule 2 requires, or delete that clause. Recompute distances from geocoded addresses. Settle the King George / King George Hub and Nordel / North Delta vocabulary before Wave 2.

finding: The pillar is the designated owner of 'worksafebc/wcb physio surrey', but its title and H1 contain no 'Surrey' (design_draft.md:181-182). All 12 Surrey location pages put ', Surrey' in the H1, and most also in the title (rule 3, :124). Central City's H1 is 'WorkSafeBC physiotherapy in Surrey City Centre'. This repeats the ICBC setup, where 'icbc physiotherapy surrey' saw 10 to 11 distinct URLs in 31 days (research/07 §3.2).
recommendation: Give the pillar a Surrey signal: a finder H2 such as 'WorkSafeBC physiotherapy in Surrey: 12 clinics' near the top, with an intro sentence. Put the neighbourhood first and keep 'Surrey' out of location-page titles, or move it to the meta description only. Track 'wcb physio surrey' with the pillar as target URL and fire the rule 4 alarm on it.

finding: The pilot cannot detect the risk this design is meant to avoid. Wave 1 is New Westminster, Richmond and Abbotsford: single-clinic cities 6 to 24 km from the nearest sibling. The ICBC failure (17 of 29 keywords ranking the wrong page) was concentrated in the Surrey cluster. Wave 2 then launches 14 pages at once, 10 of them in Surrey (design_draft.md:160). The scale rule (:163) checks indexing, G-5 rank guardrails and the rotation alarm. It does not check Google's canonical choice ('Duplicate, Google chose different canonical'), normalised similarity, or engagement. The alarm depends on SE Ranking, whose Data API subscription ends 2026-11-06 (Q-8).
recommendation: Add a Wave 1b close-pair pilot, e.g. Newton and King George (both on the cached list, 2.4 km apart). Roll out Wave 2 in batches of 2 to 3 pages with a 30-day check each. Add exit criteria per batch: each page in GSC URL Inspection is indexed with its own canonical; each page gets impressions for its own clinic-name plus WCB queries; normalised similarity stays under the ceiling. Do not start Wave 2 without working rank tracking.

scope: §5 claims policy; §4 G1; CUJ 4; data/claims-register.csv SYN-01
finding: Contract evidence is not recorded per clinic. SYN-01 is a single row, 'All Synergy Rehab clinics are WorkSafeBC-contracted...', and claims-signoff.json signs claim ids globally. Signing it to unblock Wave 1 would record that all clinics are contracted, and it unlocks the unscoped pillar SYN-08. G1 is a boolean that Marketing flips (CUJ 4, design_draft.md:86) with no vendor number, signer or date recorded. merge_locations.py sets contract_2026 to 'UNVERIFIED' as free text.
recommendation: Replace SYN-01 with per-clinic evidence: `contract_2026: {vendor_number, legal_entity, confirmed_by, date}` in worksafe-locations.json, with G1 derived from it, never set by hand. Reword SYN-01 to 'Synergy Rehab <clinic> is WorkSafeBC-contracted', with one sign-off per clinic. Pillar Synergy statements must say 'at clinics marked WorkSafeBC-contracted below'.

scope: §6.2 band 3 (WCB services), band 6 massage FAQ; §6.1 band 9; §2 WCB massage/acupuncture row
finding: WCB massage and acupuncture are offered per clinic based only on Jane appointment types. 'Yes. WCB massage follow-up visits are bookable online at X' is tagged SYN-JANE, which is OK_TO_PUBLISH. The massage card is tagged WSBC-35, also OK_TO_PUBLISH. The register itself says RMT contract status per clinic is UNKNOWN (WSBC-35 notes), that the acupuncturist's WorkSafeBC status must be confirmed (WSBC-36), and that 'Bookability is not proof of a WorkSafeBC contract' (SYN-JANE). No gate exists for these services.
recommendation: Add per-clinic service confirmations (massage_wsbc_confirmed, acupuncture_wsbc_confirmed, each with signer and date). Render the WCB massage and acupuncture cards and FAQ answers only when the confirmation is true; otherwise omit them, with no 'not online here' wording that implies coverage elsewhere.

scope: D6 (§3); §7 schema; §3 existing URL decisions; Alternatives A/D
finding: The page-per-clinic justification is gone. Research/06 §7.2 justified a page per clinic because each would be a GBP landing page with distinct facts; geo terms are all ND (114 of 114). D6 keeps GBP links on the general clinic pages (design_draft.md:141), which contradicts spec/modern-seo-cluster.md ('GBP website links point to the matching page'). With no measured demand and no GBP link, each page exists to rank for '<service> <place>' strings unless its content earns its place, which is the doorway definition. The general pages also keep their WorkSafe role: 5 clinic pages carry 'More About Worksafe' sections (research/01:133, :359) and /physiotherapy-in-new-west/ stays with its WorkSafe copy. That leaves a second WorkSafe location family, which research/07 §3.2 warned against. §7 creates a new MedicalClinic `@id` on each WorkSafe URL, giving 2 to 3 entities per physical clinic.
recommendation: State the user-value case for each page in the design: what a worker learns there that the pillar card and the general page do not. Give each clinic one entity `@id`, on its canonical general clinic page, and have the WorkSafe page reference it via about/mainEntity with a Service node. Decide per clinic whether the WorkSafe sections on general pages shrink to one sentence plus a link once the WorkSafe page is indexed. Consider linking the WorkSafe page from the GBP as a service or appointment link.

finding: The '<weekday hours summary>' uses only the first grouped hours row (location.mjs:11, 17). That produces misleading SERP snippets: Clayton Corners 'Open Mon to Tue 12 PM to 8 PM' (it is also open Wed to Fri) and Vancouver 'Open Mon 8 AM to 8 PM' (it is open Tue to Fri and Sun too).
recommendation: Generate a full summary ('Open 7 days', 'Open Mon to Fri, Sun') with the latest closing time, or drop hours from the meta description. Add a QA check comparing the meta hours text with the hours table.

finding: The gates ignore mismatches on WorkSafeBC's own provider list, which ranks #1 for 'wcb physio surrey', 'abbotsford' and 'new westminster' (research/08 bottom line 3). That list shows New Westminster (Wave 1) at unit 202 while the clinic is at #405, lists Central City as 'King George Hub' with phone 604.653.7411, and gives Vancouver a different phone (SYN-18, research/05 §6). Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners are absent. A worker who checks the official list against a page that says 'WorkSafeBC contracted' will find contradictions.
recommendation: Extend G1 or G2: the clinic's entry on the current WorkSafeBC list matches the page's name, address and phone, or a correction has been filed with WorkSafeBC and logged with a date. Until it matches, the page may show the official list link with a short note on the known discrepancy.

finding: A field listing nearby workplaces invites employer-name and industrial-area keyword stuffing, a classic doorway signal. It could also imply employer arrangements or EAPP partnerships, which are unverified (WSBC-41 STAFF_CONFIRM; Synergy on EAPP lists only LIKELY, research/05 §6). It currently counts toward G3 without rendering.
recommendation: Drop it from G3. If it is kept as copy, limit it to a generic description of the commute (e.g. 'near the Annacis Island industrial area'), with no employer names and no wording that implies a referral relationship, and send it through the claims register.

finding: The spec title formula 'WorkSafeBC Physio <Name> | WCB Physiotherapy | Synergy Rehab' does not match the build ('WCB & WorkSafeBC Physio in <place> | Synergy Rehab'). The build's length fallback drops 'Surrey' for Central City, Clayton Corners and Clayton Heights, which is inconsistent with rule 3.
recommendation: Make the spec and the build agree on one formula, and document the fallback rule explicitly.

scope: §6.1 trust tiles and title; brand rule '19+ locations'
finding: There are exactly 19 clinics. The '19+' claim is not in the claims register (research/09 P-07). In WorkSafe copy it reads as a count of WorkSafeBC clinics.
recommendation: Keep '19+ locations' for general brand lines only. In any WorkSafeBC statement, use the build-computed count of G1-true clinics.

finding: Vancouver, Burnaby and Clayton Corners each show only 2 WCB physios with openings in the sampled week, and Clayton Corners has no weekend hours (research/09 A-08). A page whose main CTA leads to little availability serves users poorly.
recommendation: Add a capacity note to the selection criteria. For low-capacity clinics, the hero should also point to the nearest G1-true clinic with openings.

finding: The pillar targets the keyword 'wcb approved physiotherapy', but nothing bans 'approved' or 'authorized' wording. That wording is already live on Yelp and was flagged by research/09 C-17 and research/06 §4.1.
recommendation: Add a banned-wording rule to §5: never 'approved', 'authorized' or 'certified'. Use 'contracted with WorkSafeBC' only after G1, and add a build lint for these words.

finding: The document says the ICBC near-duplication 'causes' URL rotation and that 17 of 29 keywords 'rank the wrong clinic's page'. Research/07 §3.2 labels the causal link a LIKELY interpretation and says the wrong page is 'usually' another clinic's.
recommendation: Use the source's hedged wording, since this premise drives the design.

scope: §6.1 Pillar (title line 181, meta 183, band 1 line 187, band 3 line 189, band 8 line 194), §2 pillar cluster (line 112), Q-1 (line 52), §4 G1 (line 145)
finding:
The pillar launches with Wave 1 and has no contract gate, yet it promotes WCB assessments at every clinic:
- Title: "WorkSafeBC Physiotherapy at 19+ Clinics".
- Meta: "Book a WCB physiotherapy assessment at one of 19+ Synergy Rehab clinics".
- Band 3: "we handle WorkSafeBC billing (SYN-08 pending G1)". G1 is undefined for the pillar.
- Band 8: a "Book WCB assessment" Jane link for every clinic that has no published page.

G1 is a per-clinic location-page gate only. build_pages.mjs line 60 checks G1 only when a clinic object is passed, and the pillar never passes one.

SYN-01 is UNVERIFIED/STAFF_CONFIRM (register line 51), and worksafe-locations.json has contract_2026=UNVERIFIED for all 19. Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners are HIGH risk and appear on no cached WorkSafeBC MSK list (research/05 lines 118, 126). WSBC-10 sends workers to a contracted physio. At a non-contracted clinic the worker pays and is reimbursed $95, covering any difference (WSBC-26).

Q-1 says it 'blocks publishing any page', which contradicts a Wave 1 pillar launch. The pillar's keyword cluster includes 'wcb approved physiotherapy', and neither '19+' nor 'approved' has a register row (research/09 C-10, C-17, P-07).
recommendation:
Add a pillar contract gate:
- Finder cards for clinics with G1=false show name, address and phone only: no WCB booking link and no WorkSafeBC wording.
- Title, meta and trust tiles use the count of G1-true clinics, or drop the count (e.g. 'WorkSafeBC Physiotherapy | WCB Physio | Synergy Rehab').
- The band 3 billing sentence appears only if every clinic shown has G1=true. Otherwise say 'clinics marked WorkSafeBC-contracted bill WorkSafeBC directly'.

Also:
- Add register rows for '19+ clinics' and 'WCB/WorkSafeBC approved' (STAFF_CONFIRM, dependent on SYN-01).
- Ban 'approved', 'official' and 'endorsed' wording and WorkSafeBC logos.
- State in Q-1 exactly which pillar elements it blocks.

finding:
'Synergy-specific statements (direct billing at this clinic, no fees at this clinic)... carry data-claim="SYN-01"' uses the wrong claim ids:
- Direct billing is SYN-08 (line 58, STAFF_CONFIRM).
- No fees is SYN-09 (line 59, STAFF_CONFIRM). Its note says: 'qualify with on an accepted claim, for your claim-related injury'.
- The no-top-up rule is WSBC-24 (line 25, STAFF_CONFIRM, agreement version uncertain).

An unqualified 'no fees at this clinic' conflicts with WSBC-28 (line 29: the clinic may ask you to pay before acceptance), WSBC-30 (line 31: pending-time treatment unpaid if the claim is denied) and WSBC-25 (areas outside the claim are billable). Tagged SYN-01, the sentence publishes as soon as G1 is true, skipping SYN-09's qualifier, WSBC-24's sign-off and Q-5.
recommendation:
Tag direct billing SYN-08, and fee statements SYN-09 plus WSBC-23/WSBC-24. Require both G1 for that clinic and each row's own sign-off.

Fixed wording: 'On an accepted claim, we bill WorkSafeBC directly for your claim-related care and you should not have to pay fees.' Never print 'no fees' or 'you pay nothing' alone. Place SYN-PEND (after Q-5) beside it.

finding:
The CUJ 2 wording matches WSBC-12 (line 13) and WSBC-29 (line 30), and both ids are correct OK_TO_PUBLISH rows. But the answer to 'can I start now' covers only the initial assessment. It omits:
- WSBC-17: funded treatment starts only on acceptance.
- WSBC-28: you may be asked to pay; the register note says Synergy's policy 'must be stated next to this'.
- WSBC-30 (STAFF_CONFIRM): if denied, pending-time treatment is not paid.
- SYN-PEND / Q-5: Synergy's own policy.
- WSBC-14: after 60 days, pre-approval, not refusal. Without it the copy invites the SYN-04 misreading (DNP/CONFLICT).

WSBC-29's note: payment depends on the clinic filing the 83D555 initial report within 7 days. Both quotes come from the provider-facing reference manual, seen only in search snippets, and the 'official source link' is not specified. Band 4 lists WSBC-11, 12, 14, 17 and 29 but not WSBC-28, WSBC-30 or SYN-PEND.
recommendation:
Rewrite the CUJ 2 Then clause to include: WSBC-12 + WSBC-29; then WSBC-17; WSBC-28; the SYN-PEND sentence (gated by Q-5); and WSBC-14.

- Link the Feb 2026 Reference Manual for WSBC-12/29 and the Health care benefits page for WSBC-28.
- Require staff to confirm both manual quotes on the live document.
- Add to Q-5: Synergy never charges for the initial assessment on a pending claim within 60 days, and files 83D555 within 7 days.
- Add WSBC-28, WSBC-30 and SYN-PEND to bands 2 and 4.

finding:
The CUJ 1 worker was hurt yesterday and has not reported to WorkSafeBC, yet the path ends 'bring your claim number', and the location meta says 'Bring your WorkSafeBC claim number.'
- WSBC-46 (line 47): the number arrives by mail after the report.
- WSBC-11/12/13 allow the assessment while the claim is pending.
- SYN-07's note says to add 'your claim can still be pending'.

On Teleclaim, the CUJ shows only 1.888.967.5377. WSBC-44 (line 45) gives 604.231.8888 for the Lower Mainland, which includes New Westminster, and Mon-Fri 8-6 hours. WSBC-43 (line 44) recommends reporting online (24/7) for a single-incident physical injury, which this lifting back strain is.

The build already shows the drift:
- location.mjs line 147: 'Bring your 8-digit claim number'.
- line 145: toll-free number only.
- The pillar tip says choosing 'WCB Physio Initial Session' sets the visit up 'as a WorkSafeBC claim'. A Jane booking creates no claim.
recommendation:
CUJ 1 Then clause:
- Report online 24/7 (recommended for this injury) or call Teleclaim at 604.231.8888 / 1.888.967.5377, Mon-Fri 8-6 (WSBC-43/44).
- You can book before the claim number arrives; bring it if you have it (WSBC-46, WSBC-11).

Also:
- Change the location meta to 'Bring your claim number if you have it.'
- Ban any wording that implies booking in Jane opens a WorkSafeBC claim.

scope: Q-4 (line 55), pillar band 2 referral answer (line 188), Problem 4 (line 24)
finding:
Q-4 asks staff to 'Confirm WSBC-16 (no doctor's referral needed)'. WSBC-16 (line 17) is PARTIAL: 'No official snippet states this for physiotherapy... Publish the WSBC-10 wording instead of an absolute no referral needed.' SYN-06 says the same. A staff name and date is not an official source, so this breaks the spec's own rule that every fact traces to a dated official source (line 27).

The build already prints 'Not for physiotherapy.' (pillar.mjs line 102).

Problem 4 calls the competitors' 'referral after 60 days' rule 'incorrect', but research/08 line 87 rates this LIKELY. WSBC-14 shows only that pre-approval is needed, and no source says a referral is not needed after 60 days.
recommendation:
Reword Q-4: 'find an official worksafebc.com sentence for WSBC-16; if none, use WSBC-10 wording'.

Referral answer: 'WorkSafeBC tells workers to go to a contracted physiotherapist and say the injury is work-related (WSBC-10). Massage is different: it needs a doctor's referral (WSBC-35).'

Reword Problem 4 to 'not supported by current WorkSafeBC sources'.

scope: Pillar band 4 have-ready checklist (line 190), band 6 first visit (line 192)
finding:
The have-ready checklist uses WSBC-49. WSBC-49 (line 50) lists what to have ready when reporting to WorkSafeBC, including employer details, PHN, earnings for the past 12 weeks and SIN. It is PARTIAL/STAFF_CONFIRM, and its note says 'Link to the official page rather than reproducing the list.' research/09 P-07 (line 172) flagged the same mix-up.

Using it as a checklist for the physio visit is the wrong claim id and could prompt workers to bring their SIN or earnings. Band 6 ('what to bring') has no claim id at all.
recommendation:
Split the checklist in two:
- A link: 'Reporting to WorkSafeBC? See what to have ready', pointing to the how-workers-report page (no list reproduced).
- A clinic-visit checklist as a new Synergy ops row (e.g. SYN-BRING, STAFF_CONFIRM): claim number if you have it, employer name, injury date, PHN or photo ID. Ops signs it off.

Never list SIN or earnings.

finding:
