Band 7 tags 'reports to WorkSafeBC' with WSBC-21, but WSBC-21 (line 22) is about requesting more treatment. The report forms are WSBC-05, which is DNP and provider-internal.

The RTW article covers modified duties and communication with the employer and WorkSafeBC, yet the register has no return-to-work rows at all. Reviewer knowledge, to verify: since January 1, 2024 the BC Workers Compensation Act has included a duty to cooperate and a duty to maintain employment, which a 2026 modified-duties article must reflect.

'Goals tied to job demands' edges toward RTWSS and CRRTW services. Synergy is not on the RTWSS list (research/05 lines 133, 146), WSBC-40 is DNP, and the SYN-12 'OR1 & OR2' bio is DNP.
recommendation:
Before drafting RTW content:
- Add register rows sourced from worksafebc.com return-to-work pages: worker and employer duties, who decides RTW, modified duties.
- Tag every sentence.
- Retag or delete 'reports to WorkSafeBC'.
- Add a rule: no wording that implies Synergy delivers CRRTW, RTWSS, OR1/OR2 or EAPP programs.

finding:
WCB massage (9 clinics) and WCB acupuncture (Nordel) are promoted wherever Jane shows them bookable. But:
- SYN-JANE (line 70): 'Bookability is not proof of a WorkSafeBC contract'.
- WSBC-35 note: RMT contract status per clinic is UNKNOWN.
- WSBC-36 note: confirm the acupuncturist's status.
- Jane offers only 'WCB Massage Subsequent Session', so there is no first-visit booking path (research/04 line 11; research/09 C-16).
- The concurrent-care rule (research/05 line 149: one therapy type at a time, LIKELY) is not in the register, yet the spec offers massage and acupuncture beside physio.

No gate covers any of this; G1 covers physio only.
recommendation:
Add per-clinic STAFF_CONFIRM rows (e.g. SYN-RMT-<slug>, SYN-ACU-nordel) and a service gate. Show a service only when its row is signed.

- Add a concurrent-care row sourced from 'Your Claim: Helpful Information'. Until it is verified, no 'alongside physio' wording.
- For massage, say 'call the clinic to book your first WCB massage visit', or omit the CTA.

finding:
(a) 'A staff member opens each cited official URL' is not recorded or enforced. claims-signoff.json has one checked_as_of field and a signed map for STAFF_CONFIRM rows only. All 23 OK_TO_PUBLISH rows are snippet-only (research/05 line 19), and publish mode does not fail on an unchecked OK row.

(b) Usage conditions in the notes of OK rows are not enforced: WSBC-11 (Synergy wording needs SYN-01), WSBC-26 (no gap implication), WSBC-28 (pending policy beside it), WSBC-01 (context line only).

(c) A name plus a date can unlock STAFF_CONFIRM rows with CONFLICT/UNVERIFIED status. Examples: SYN-17 ('never cite it as a Synergy listing') and SYN-18. The same applies to WSBC-18, which must be checked against the signed 2026 agreement schedule. No document reference is required.

(d) The title, meta and JSON-LD carry no data-claim, and untagged sentences pass undetected, e.g. pillar.mjs 'WorkSafeBC sets the length of each treatment period'. G-4 cannot be measured.
recommendation:
Record per claim used, OK rows included: {url_opened, quote_matches, checked_on, by, evidence_doc_section}. Fail publish if any field is missing or quote_matches is false.

- Add a copy_eligible allow-list so SYN-16, SYN-17 and SYN-18 can never render.
- Encode co-occurrence rules, e.g. WSBC-28 requires SYN-PEND.
- Add claim annotations to meta.json and schema.json, and list them in qa-report.
- Have a reviewer read every page for untagged WorkSafeBC sentences.

finding:
SYN-01 (line 51) reads 'All Synergy Rehab clinics are WorkSafeBC-contracted', but the spec uses it as a per-clinic gate. claims-signoff.json keys sign-offs by claim id only.

Signing SYN-01 therefore attests all 19 clinics, including the HIGH-risk ones, while G1 lives separately in worksafe-locations.json, giving two sources of truth. A single global SYN-08 sign-off would unlock the pillar's 'we bill WorkSafeBC' for every clinic.
recommendation: Split into per-clinic rows (SYN-01-<slug>) holding legal entity, vendor/payee number and the date checked, and derive G1 from them. Pillar statements that need SYN-01/SYN-08 require every listed clinic to be signed.

finding:
fragment.html is written in every mode and labelled '(paste into WordPress)', while preview mode allows unsigned STAFF_CONFIRM claims.

The current pages/dist/qa-report.json is mode=preview. The pillar fragment carries 7 pending claims (GEN-01, WSBC-16, SYN-PEND, WSBC-30, SYN-08, WSBC-49, WSBC-36) as normal visible text, marked only by a data attribute that is invisible without the preview CSS. Pasting it would publish unsigned claims.
recommendation: Emit fragment.html only in publish mode. Preview mode writes preview.html, plus, if needed, a fragment with a visible in-fragment 'DRAFT: NOT FOR PUBLISHING' watermark. The RUNBOOK must require qa-report mode=publish before anything is pasted.

finding:
The coverage guide owns the riskiest topics:
- user fees: WSBC-24, SYN-09 (STAFF_CONFIRM)
- extensions: WSBC-20 (STAFF_CONFIRM, with visit numbers)
- pending claims: WSBC-30/31 (STAFF_CONFIRM)
- Form 6: WSBC-48 (STAFF_CONFIRM); Form 6A (research/05 line 163) has no row

Yet it is 'delivered as a separate file for the content owner' outside the build's publish gate.

Its live copy includes SYN-10, SYN-13 (chiropractic needs no referral; WorkSafeBC chiropractic is not offered, WSBC-08 DNP), SYN-14 (mileage, DNP/UNVERIFIED) and SYN-15. The spec names only the SYN-11 fix.
recommendation: Put the coverage guide (and the RTW article) through the same build: data-claim tags, publish mode and sign-off. List the removals explicitly: SYN-04, SYN-13 chiropractic lines, SYN-14 mileage, SYN-15. Add register rows for Form 6A and for any claim-process fact the guide answers.

finding:
Known-wrong WorkSafeBC copy stays live after launch:
- /icbc-claims/: the SYN-04 60-day misstatement (DNP/CONFLICT, KNOWN verbatim) is not listed, and the SYN-03 fix is left as an 'owner decision'.
- Homepage: it also repeats SYN-04 (research/02 line 77), but only SYN-02 is listed.
- King George and Delta general pages: '15 sessions' (SYN-03, DNP) is fixed only 'when each clinic page launches', i.e. Wave 2.
- /physiotherapy-in-new-west/: 'Keep unchanged', though it was never crawled (research/01 lines 261, 402), so its WorkSafeBC claims are unaudited. It is the page cited by AI Overviews in the pilot market.
- Not mentioned at all: the Jane SYN-12 bio, Yelp's 'Approved Physiotherapy' (research/09 C-17) and the 2023 15/6 graphic (research/09 P-08).
recommendation:
Make a pre-launch cleanup list with owners, independent of waves:
- Remove SYN-03 and SYN-04 everywhere before the pillar launches.
- Audit /physiotherapy-in-new-west/ for WorkSafeBC statements and fix any DNP copy, keeping the URL.
- Add Jane bio, Yelp, Medimap and graphic fixes as tracked tasks.

scope: §1 'official links out: provider lists' (line 99), band 11 (line 197), Wave 1 New Westminster
finding:
The WSBC-33 note says the contracted-provider-list target URL never surfaced; only a sitecore variant did. pages/src/shared.mjs line 14 links exactly that unverified URL.

The indexed lists predate April 2026 and conflict with Synergy NAP (SYN-18, line 68). New Westminster, a Wave 1 clinic, appears at unit 202 against GBP #405, and Central City is listed as 'King George Hub'. The spec never mentions SYN-18, and G1/G2 do not check the WorkSafeBC vendor record.
recommendation: Link only URLs a staff member has opened, and record each in the sign-off file. Do not tell workers to check the provider list until a post-April-2026 list shows the clinic correctly. Add to G1: the WorkSafeBC vendor record name and address match the signed-off NAP, or a correction request has been sent (SYN-18).

finding:
design-system.md still says every factual slot must map to a claim with status VERIFIED (lines 357, 704, 732). It also requires a 'VERIFIED status pill' or badge in the location hero (lines 291, 340) and keeps contested items out until VERIFIED (line 453).

Spec §5 gates on publish_rule instead (research/09 C-25), and the conflict is unresolved. The pill's text is undefined; read as 'WorkSafeBC verified/contracted' it is a SYN-01 claim.
recommendation: State in §5 that it overrides the design-system claim rules, and update design-system.md. Either define the pill as 'WorkSafeBC-contracted clinic' tagged SYN-01-<slug>, shown only when G1 is true, or remove it.

finding:
Dated WorkSafeBC facts have no re-verification cadence or expiry:
- WSBC-26: the $95 reimbursement is 'effective April 1, 2026'.
- The fee schedule window runs April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, with CPI after (WSBC-27 note).
- WSBC-44 Teleclaim hours.
- WSBC-18 is still pending.

The cadence (days 7, 30, 60, 90) has no claim re-check, so the 'accurate, dated' advantage decays silently.
recommendation: Add an expires_on field per claim (2027-03-31 for rate-bearing rows) and make the build fail past it. Re-check quarterly and on every new WorkSafeBC physiotherapy bulletin. Re-date the as-of line only after a re-check.

finding: '0 visit-count statements until WSBC-18' is ambiguous next to the planned WSBC-35 massage counts (6 treatments in 8 weeks), WSBC-36 acupuncture counts (8 visits in 8 weeks, STAFF_CONFIRM) and WSBC-20 extensions. The meta promises 'How claims, visits and costs work', which the page cannot answer with numbers.
recommendation: Scope the rule: 'no physio treatment-period or extension counts until WSBC-18/WSBC-20 are signed; WSBC-35 allowed'. Change the meta to 'How claims and costs work'.

finding: GEN-01 (line 69) was 'added by spec author; not opened' and is not in research/05. The register now has 70 rows (GEN-01, SYN-JANE and SYN-PEND added); research/05 line 4 and design-system E13 say 67. The spec does not disclose the additions.
recommendation: Note the three added rows in the spec. Source GEN-01 to the WorkSafeBC about page or the Workers Compensation Act, and sign it off like any other row.

finding:
Several planned AEO questions have no register row:
- 'How long does a WorkSafeBC claim take?' (06 §7.6 Q6)
- Form 6A (06 §4.4)
- 'Will WCB pay for physiotherapy' framing from People Also Ask

The spec says only 'each tagged'.
recommendation: List the 8 to 10 FAQ questions in the spec with their claim ids. Drop any question with no OK or signed row, or add the row first.

finding: CUJ 2 lands the pending-claim query on the pillar FAQ, but §2 assigns pending-claim questions to the coverage guide, with the pillar giving only 1 to 2 sentences.
recommendation: Choose one owner. If it is the guide, CUJ 2 should land there and link back to the finder; if the pillar, update the §2 row.

finding: Problem 4 states that competitors publish an 'incorrect' referral-after-60-days rule. research/08 rates this LIKELY, and the counter-evidence (WSBC-14: pre-approval) does not prove that no referral is needed.
recommendation: Reword to 'publish rules not supported by current WorkSafeBC sources (pre-approval after 60 days, WSBC-14)'.

finding: The pillar title 'WorkSafeBC Physiotherapy (WCB) at 19+ Clinics' and the meta 'Book a WCB physiotherapy assessment at one of 19+ Synergy Rehab clinics' (pages/src/pillar.mjs lines 7-8, also copied into MedicalWebPage name/description) assert SYN-01, which is UNVERIFIED for all 19 clinics. Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners are HIGH eligibility risk (not on cached WorkSafeBC lists; Clayton Corners Jane shows 'No Direct Billing Physiotherapy'). SYN-JANE says 'Bookability is not proof of a WorkSafeBC contract'. The build gates claims only in body HTML via ctx.claim(); write() (build_pages.mjs 179-190) checks title and meta for length and dashes only. This breaks G-4 and the research/06 §4.1 compliance flag.
recommendation: Compute the clinic count from G1-true clinics, or use a count-free title until Q-1 is answered. Add a claims[] array to meta.json and make publish mode run title, meta and every JSON-LD string through the same claim gate.

finding: The coverage guide keeps 'WorkSafeBC physiotherapy' in its title. research/06 §7.2 says to retitle it away from the head term, and research/01 §5.2 rates it High risk. Its live rankings are for queries §2 assigns elsewhere: worksafebc physiotherapy surrey #10 (pillar-owned), new westminster #4 (location-owned), Burnaby #7, Langley #9/#10 (research/08 F7). The D1/Alt-B premise that the head terms show a local pack is wrong for 'worksafebc physiotherapy': the live SERP (task 264768352) had no pack, worksafebc.com held 5 of 10, and research/06 §4.1 says only the wcb/approved variants show a pack.
recommendation: Record an explicit owner decision (research/09 C-18). If the guide stays separate, retitle it to lead with the coverage questions and list it in §2 as a monitored competitor for head and city terms. Include it in rule-4 alternation monitoring and decide whether G-1 credits it.

finding: research/01 §0 says schema is Not Available for every URL and 'needs a structured-data crawl before any schema decisions'; the design skips that audit. The duplicate canonical on 388 pages points to two SEO emitters that likely output their own graphs. The build hard-codes /#organization, /#website (build_pages.mjs lines 108, 117) and {url}#webpage, the default @id patterns of common WP SEO plugins, which risks merged or conflicting nodes and duplicate BreadcrumbLists. Location pages reference #organization and #website, which exist only on the pillar, and Google reads each page's markup on its own. The design (Organization with logo and telephone, WebPage with dateModified) also differs from the build (MedicalOrganization without them, MedicalWebPage without dateModified, FAQPage always emitted).
recommendation: Before launch, view the source of a drafted page and list every ld+json block. Then extend the plugin graph using its @ids, or disable plugin schema on WorkSafe URLs. Put a minimal Organization node (name, url, logo, sameAs) on every page. Validate the fully rendered source in Rich Results Test code mode (drafts cannot be fetched). Bring §7 in line with the build.

finding: The clinic node's @id and url are the WorkSafe page (build_pages.mjs line 126), while D6 keeps GBP website links on the general clinic pages or the homepage. Any future LocalBusiness markup on general pages would create a second entity for the same clinic. There is no sameAs to the GBP, although modern-seo-cluster.md (Entity signals) and research/09 B-13 require it. hasMap can never be emitted because worksafe-locations.json has no Maps URL or CID field (research/04 knows CIDs for 3 clinics).
recommendation: Use stable site-level IDs (https://synergyrehabilitation.ca/#clinic-<slug>) with url set to the GBP website target, and have the WorkSafe WebPage point to it via about. Add gbp.maps_url and gbp.cid to the data and emit hasMap and sameAs. Reuse the same IDs in the pillar finder (ItemList) and later on general pages.

finding: The duplicate canonical (388 pages), duplicate meta description (82) and h1_multiple (106) are noted as 'must be fixed site-wide' with no owner, date or gate. The new pages inherit them. The auto-generated second description takes the first body text, which on these fragments is the breadcrumb ('Home WorkSafeBC physiotherapy New Westminster...'). The build counts H1s only inside the fragment, and the runbook checks 'canonical' but not that there is exactly one.
recommendation: Find the two emitters and disable one before the pillar launches; make it a G4 sub-check. After publishing, assert on the rendered HTML: exactly 1 rel=canonical (self), 1 meta description, 1 H1, 1 BreadcrumbList, and robots set to index.

finding: The doc's pillar title is 68 chars, so its fallback always fires and the result drops 'WCB' (wcb physiotherapy, 210/mo, is the largest term; research/06 §7.5 says use both names). The doc's location meta formula gives 156-177 chars (16 of 19 over the build's 165 limit) and has no shortening rule. The build ships different formulas (location.mjs 7-21). Its hours summary uses only the first day group: 'Open Mon 8 AM to 8 PM' (Vancouver), 'Open Mon to Tue 12 PM to 8 PM' (Clayton Corners), 'Open Mon to Wed' (Cloverdale). The fallback above 62 chars drops 'Surrey' for 5 Surrey clinics. Titles use the display name, not area_label (Central City vs H1 Surrey City Centre; Clayton Corners vs East Clayton; Delta vs North Delta), breaking §2 rules 2 and 3.
recommendation: Replace §6.1/§6.2 with the formulas the build actually uses, with limits in characters and pixels. Build the hours phrase from all 7 days ('Open 7 days, evenings to 8:30 PM') or drop it. Use area_label the same way in title, H1 and meta, and add QA assertions for both.

finding: The pillar owns worksafebc/wcb physio surrey, but rule 3 puts 'Surrey' in every Surrey location page's title, H1 and meta (7 built titles end ', Surrey'), and the pillar's own title has no 'Surrey'. ICBC precedent (research/07 §3.2): 'icbc physiotherapy surrey' used 10-11 Synergy URLs in 31 days, and 'icbc massage therapy surrey' rotated 5 location pages. 12 Surrey pages plus the pillar will compete for the same query.
recommendation: Keep 'Surrey' in H1, address and breadcrumb but remove it from Surrey location titles. Give the pillar a Surrey H2 and a finder anchor. Track wcb physio surrey and worksafebc physiotherapy surrey with the pillar as target URL under the rule-4 alarm.

finding: The /physiotherapy-in-new-west/ row says 'Keep unchanged' and also 'add one in-body link' (contradictory), and has no branch for the old page continuing to outrank the new one, which fails G-2 in New Westminster with no remedy. Its '2 AI Overviews' claim rests on domain-level citations only (research/08 lines 1132, 1153). Not addressed: /physiotherapy-abbotsford-chiropractor/ (Abbotsford GBP landing, 38 in-links, 'More About Worksafe' and 'Worksafe Injury Physiotherapy' sections; research/07 medium risk); /richmond-physiotherapy-2/ (#7 wcb physio richmond, duplicate of /richmond-physiotherapy/); /icbc-physiotherapy-abbotsford/ (#11, frozen, no cross-link). research/07 §3.2 warns against leaving a second indexable WorkSafe location family.
recommendation: Add rows for each URL. Cut the WorkSafe sections on the 5 newer clinic pages to one sentence plus a link. Decide the -2 duplicate (canonical to the main page or noindex). Add a G-2 failure branch at day 60 (narrow or retitle the legacy page). Ask the owner whether a one-line 'Injured at work?' pointer is allowed on the ICBC Richmond and Abbotsford pages.

finding: data/worksafe-locations.json has 16 nearby entries with slug null across 15 of 19 clinics. The regex in build/merge_locations.py line 54 ('0\d (.+?) About ([\d.]+) km') swallows address text. Examples: Nordel loses Central City (3.0 km), Vancouver and Burnaby lose Delta, Newton loses Sullivan Heights and Strawberry Hill. location.mjs line 65 ('if (!t) return') drops them silently, so most nearby blocks render 2-3 links instead of 4.
recommendation: Fix the parser (match against the known clinic-name list, or compute distances from coordinates). Make the QA report fail on any null slug or on fewer than 4 nearby links per page.

finding: The uniqueness test is a manual judgment. qa-report.json already shows max 5-word-shingle Jaccard of 0.42-0.53 between location pages, yet near-duplicate templates are the doc's stated main risk (Problem 5) and no numeric threshold blocks publishing.
recommendation: Add a numeric publish blocker, e.g. max Jaccard <= 0.30 against any sibling once staff facts are filled, alongside the manual band-removal test.

finding: G-3 requires events per 100 organic sessions, reported weekly from launch. research/07 §5 and finding 7 say GA4 is Not Available (no connector, Supermetrics LICENSE_NOT_FOUND, configuration UNKNOWN) and bookings happen on Jane, a separate domain. The runbook's GA4 DebugView and GSC URL Inspection checks need access that research/07 §4.5 and research/09 say does not exist. No open question covers GA4, GTM or GSC access.
recommendation: Add a Q-11 for GA4, GTM and GSC access with an owner. Make it a launch prerequisite for G-3 and for the day-7 and day-30 indexing checks. Until then, state G-3 as 'not measurable'.

finding: A +/-3 band around a single-day baseline cannot hold against observed 30-day volatility in data/rank-baseline.csv: icbc physiotherapy Delta best 1/worst 80, icbc physio New West 2/72, car accident physiotherapy Langley 3/75. Most generic 'physiotherapy <city>' terms are not tracked on the 9 engines; the rows that exist are GSC averages with no engine, or path-scoped project 12940679 rows. Because Wave 2 is gated on 'no G-5 regressions', noise alone would stall it.
recommendation: Compare the 14-day median before launch with the 14-day median after. Count a regression only when the ranking URL switches to a WorkSafe page (research/07 §7E alert rule). Add the 9 generic guardrail pairs at least 2 weeks before launch.

finding: G-1's 'Baseline: 0 of 9 (research/07)' was never measured; research/07 says 'There is no rank-tracking baseline for WorkSafe today'. The 12903890 engines are 'map merged', so their top 10 is not an organic top 10, and it is unclear whether one keyword or both must rank on an engine. G-2 uses 'wcb physio <city>', which is not in the research/07 §7C set adopted in §9 (that set has wcb physiotherapy <city> and worksafe physio <city>). G-6: per-prompt AI tracker results came back null (research/07 §6), the AIO engine exists only in the path-scoped project, no engine is named, and data/ai-visibility-log.csv (modern-seo-cluster.md) does not exist.
recommendation: Take the G-1 baseline from 14 days of tracking before launch, define positions as organic with the pack excluded, and state AND or OR. Add 'wcb physio <city>' to the tracking set. For G-6, name the engine (ChatGPT 155491, or add AIO to 12903890) and the metric, and keep a manual monthly answer log.

finding: Publish gate G5 and goals G-1, G-2, G-5, G-6 and rule 4 all depend on SE Ranking. research/07 says the Data API subscription expires 2026-11-06 21:34, whether rank tracking stops with it is UNKNOWN, and keywords should be added at least 2 weeks before launch. If tracking lapses, no page can pass G5 and no goal can be scored.
recommendation: Make SE Ranking renewal (or a named replacement tracker) an explicit launch prerequisite with an owner and date. Get Q-8 approved now so the 14-day baseline exists before Wave 1.

finding: modern-seo-cluster.md says every pillar and location page must pass each row before publish, including INP < 200 ms, 'One primary keyword per URL from keyword-master.csv' and sameAs to the GBP. The design says INP is 'reported, not promised'; origin INP fails (19-20% poor, about 3.8 MB of theme JS, research/01 §3 rows 19-20); all 508 keyword-master rows have URL Target 'Not Available'; §7 has no sameAs. As written, no page can pass its acceptance checklist.
recommendation: Amend the checklist's INP row to 'reported' for theme-driven INP, or add a site-wide JS remediation gate. Write the §2 owner map into the URL Target column of keyword-master.csv. Add sameAs to §7.

finding: The design's Organization telephone would be the 'main line', which matches Nordel's clinic phone (nap_conflicts: 'Clinic phone equals the corporate main line'). The build names it 'Synergy Rehabilitation' while GBP names use 'Synergy Rehab'. Organization is declared on a service pillar rather than the homepage.
recommendation: Declare Organization on the homepage (or reuse the plugin's node) with alternateName 'Synergy Rehab', and use a corporate number distinct from any clinic, or omit telephone.

finding: availableService is a generic MedicalTherapy named 'WorkSafeBC (WCB) physiotherapy', but WorkSafeBC is a payer, not a therapy. dateModified (listed in the design) is missing from the build. The reviewer line is not reflected in the markup.
recommendation: Type availableService as PhysicalTherapy named 'Physiotherapy'. Add lastReviewed and reviewedBy to MedicalWebPage, filled from claims-signoff.json, and restore dateModified.

finding: The design calls pillar FAQPage optional, but the build always emits it (build_pages.mjs line 120). Its JSON-LD answer text carries no visible data-claim markers, so a reviewer cannot see claim status there.
recommendation: Decide whether FAQPage ships. If it does, have publish mode refuse it when any FAQ answer uses an unsigned STAFF_CONFIRM claim; the build already records these, so assert it.

finding: The only sitemap mention is a post-publish 'sitemap inclusion' check. There are no rules for lastmod, for excluding gated drafts, or for dropping /tag/worksafebc/ once noindexed. GSC sitemap submission needs GSC access, which is not available.
recommendation: Add a sitemap subsection: pillar and published children included with lastmod; drafts and the noindexed tag archive excluded; submit and inspect in GSC once access exists (Q-11).

finding: /tag/worksafebc/ is missing from data/site-urls.csv, so its status, canonical and indexability are unknown (research/09 B-09). A global 'noindex tags' setting would also hit /tag/abbotsford/, which ranks for an ICBC term.
recommendation: Check its live status first. Apply a per-term noindex,follow rather than the global tag-archive setting.

finding: 'No redirects are created in this project' means a location page rolled back after indexing returns 404 and loses any links and signals it earned.
recommendation: Allow a 301 from a withdrawn location page to /worksafe-physiotherapy/#clinics, or use a deliberate 410 and remove the page from the sitemap.

finding: The build's finder and nearby anchors are 'Synergy Rehab <Name>', not '<Name> clinic' or '<Name>, <distance> km'. Close siblings are named outside the nearby block (the Newton page names King George 4 times; local FAQs name the nearest clinics), contrary to rule 2.
recommendation: Bring §8 in line with the build, or the build in line with §8. Relax rule 2 to 'nearby block and the full-clinic FAQ only', or remove sibling names from the FAQs.

finding: /locations/ (363 in-links) and /booking-page/ (748) are not in the linking plan. research/01 §5.3 point 2 says location pages need links in from the clinic page, /locations/ and the hub.
recommendation: Add /locations/ to pillar and /locations/ to each published WorkSafe page rows (with owner approval if those templates are shared).

finding: The built pillar links twice to /return-to-work-after-a-workplace-injury/ (pillar.mjs lines 199, 249). That article is not built and needs clinical sign-off, so the links 404 if the pillar launches first. The build does not validate internal link targets.
recommendation: Have the build emit internal links only to URLs in a live-URL allowlist, or ship the RTW article with the pillar.

finding: 'Abbotsford and New Westminster have GBP data connected… so Maps effects can be measured' overstates it. Abbotsford is connected but has no WorkSafe keyword in its Local grid (gbp-maps-keyword-positions.csv; research/04 'No WorkSafe/WCB keyword in Maps rank tracking'), and D6 keeps the GBP website on the general page.
recommendation: Add 'wcb physiotherapy' and 'worksafe physiotherapy' to the Abbotsford and New Westminster Local grids under Q-8, and say Maps effects are indirect under D6.

finding: Schema NAP and openingHoursSpecification come from the client Yelp sheet, which conflicts with GBP and site values for several clinics: postal codes for Abbotsford, Newton, Richmond, Delta and Central City; Newton and Richmond hours (research/09 C-04, C-07). G2 is a boolean set by marketing, and nothing cross-checks schema against the GBP.
recommendation: Make G2 sign-off explicitly 'matches GBP', record the GBP values in the data, and have the build fail if the schema differs from the signed-off record.

scope: 6.1 bands 1 and 8; 6.2 bands 6-7; section 4 gates; Q-1
finding: Only location pages are protected by the G1 contract gate. The pillar is not. These all imply a WorkSafeBC contract at every clinic: the title 'WorkSafeBC Physiotherapy at 19+ Clinics' (line 181), the meta (183), the trust tile (187), and finder cards that give every unpublished clinic a 'Book WCB assessment' Jane link (194). On location pages, the nearby block and the local FAQ answer 'nearest clinic if this one is full' (213-214) do the same. But worksafe-locations.json has contract_2026 = UNVERIFIED for all 19 clinics. Cedar Hills (line 781) and Clayton Corners (line 1906) are eligibility_risk HIGH: not on cached WorkSafeBC lists, and Medimap lists Cedar Hills as private pay (SYN-16). SYN-JANE says bookability is not proof of a contract. The build confirms it: pages/src/pillar.mjs finder() (lines 40-53) never checks gates in any mode. Built New Westminster sends overflow to Cedar Hills' 442 link; built Abbotsford sends it to Clayton Corners. The pillar lede places WSBC-10 ('see a contracted physiotherapist') next to 'at any of our 19+ locations'. Harm: at a non-contracted clinic the worker pays and is reimbursed at $95, paying the gap themselves (WSBC-26), and the pending-claim assessment guarantee (WSBC-29) does not apply. Q-1 says it 'blocks publishing any page', but sections 4 and 6.1 do not apply it to the pillar.
recommendation: Apply G1 per clinic wherever a clinic is offered for WCB booking: the pillar finder, the nearby block and the local FAQ. Clinics with G1 false get no Jane WCB link: either omit them, or show a card with 'Call to confirm WorkSafeBC billing'. Derive WCB-availability counts from G1-true clinics only. Do not publish the pillar until Q-1 is answered for every clinic it lists. Make publish mode fail when a clinic with G1 false gets a 442 link.

finding: The nearby data is corrupted: 16 entries across 15 of 19 clinics have slug null and names like 'Street, Unit A130, Langley Twp ; 02 Clayton Heights' (worksafe-locations.json line 2104). The cause is the merge_locations.py km_list regex '0\d (.+?) About' (lines 52-56), which matches digit pairs inside street numbers. The built Abbotsford page, a Wave 1 pilot, prints this in its local FAQ (pages/dist/abbotsford/fragment.html line 98): 'Langley (about 24 km) and Street, Unit A130, Langley Twp ; 02 Clayton Heights (about 25 km)'. Newton is the same. The nearby cards drop the bad entry silently, so Abbotsford's cards skip Clayton Heights. Publish mode does not check any of this, and the doc marks Step 1 done.
recommendation: Rewrite the parser to work from the clinic-name token list or from structured data, and map every name to a known slug. Fail the build when any nearby slug is null or unknown, and add this check to the Step 4 QA list. Re-run the merge and the previews.

scope: Jane deep links (lines 11, 69, 244); Open Questions; Step 4 QA (line 333)
finding: 442 exists at all 19 clinics (data branch), but the doc's handling of it falls short in four ways. (a) research/04 line 200 and research/09 C-24 rate 'the link opens the type directly' as only LIKELY, yet CUJ 1 states it as fact. (b) Duplicate 'WCB Physio Initial Session' IDs hide availability from the 442 link, measured over slots 2026-11-02 to 11-08. New Westminster (pilot, CUJ 1): ID 1013 covers 1 of 4 WCB physiotherapists and 20 of 70 initial slots. Newton: IDs 1019/1099/1111 cover 3 physiotherapists and 66 of 187 slots. Richmond (pilot): ID 1081 '(40 mins)', 6 slots. Langley: ID 948, 3 slots. South Surrey: ID 968, 7 slots. (c) If the hash route fails, the same booking page at Vancouver, Burnaby, New Westminster and Clayton Corners also lists 'No Direct Billing Physiotherapy' (locations-master.csv). (d) research/09 staff question 6 (which initial type each clinic's CTA should open) is missing from Q-1 to Q-10. QA checks only the slug.
recommendation: Add Q-11 for ops: consolidate the WCB initial types into one ID per clinic, or name the ID each clinic should use. The build reads per-clinic IDs and openings from the latest data branch and fails if 442 is absent or has 0 openings over 14 days. Before launch, test each Wave 1 link by hand in iOS Safari, Android Chrome and the Instagram/Facebook in-app browsers, logged out. Add microcopy under each Book CTA: 'Opens Jane. Choose WCB Physio Initial Session.'

finding: Measured on the built New Westminster preview at 390x664 px, roughly the visible area of iPhone Safari: the hero is 1,348 px tall. Book sits at 661-729 px and Call (the phone) at 741-793 px, under a 151 px mock header, so with a real header the phone is at or below the fold. The 3-step path is inside band 4 and starts 3,468 px down (about 5 screens), not 'within one scroll'. The CUJ 1 worker has not reported the injury yet, but nothing near the CTA says to (WSBC-13 needs a claim; Teleclaim WSBC-44 is in band 4). The doc has no above-the-fold requirement, and Step 4 QA checks only horizontal scroll.
recommendation: Set a fold budget: at 390x664 with the real theme header, the H1, a lede of 20 words or fewer, Book and Call must be fully visible. Add this check to screenshot.mjs. Move the 3 compact steps to band 2, directly under the hero, as design-system section 8.3 does. Add one line under the CTAs: 'Not reported yet? Report online or call Teleclaim 1.888.967.5377. You can still book now.' with a tel: link. Remove the eyebrow that repeats the clinic name, and use a shorter or landscape hero crop below 600 px.

scope: 6.1 band 1 primary CTA and band 8 clinic finder (lines 187, 194); CUJ 3
finding: 'Find your clinic' is the right primary CTA, because the pillar has no single booking target and the Jane root page exposes non-WCB and No Direct Billing types. The path behind it is too long. At 390 px the finder starts 8,258 px down a 16,086 px page and is 4,219 px tall; Surrey's 12 cards alone take about 2,600 px. Pilot clinics route pillar, then location page, then Jane: one more page load on a site with about 3.8 MB of JavaScript and 19% of mobile interactions rated poor (INP, research/01 line 258). Unpublished clinics go straight to Jane. The cards are stretched-link cards (worksafe.css line 324 overlay, z-index 2) with the phone printed as plain text (pillar.mjs line 50), so tapping the number opens Jane instead of the dialer.
recommendation: Keep 'Find your clinic'. Move the finder to band 2 or 3, or add five area chips under the hero CTA that jump to each group. On phones, render compact rows (name, neighbourhood, street) with two explicit actions: 'Book WCB physio' (Jane, G1-true clinics only) and a tel: link. When a WorkSafe page exists, link the clinic name to it, which keeps the section 8 internal link without adding a step before booking. Drop the stretched-link pattern on finder cards.

scope: 6.1 band 1 and band 12: 'call button to the main line'
finding: The doc never defines the main line. The only corporate number in the data, (604) 503-1688, is Nordel's clinic phone (research/04 lines 56 and 212; WorkSafeBC provider-list row in research/05 line 117), so pillar callers from Abbotsford or Vancouver would reach Nordel. Phone is the main contact path: Newton's GBP gets 645-758 calls a month against 14-357 website clicks (research/04 section 1.6). The build dropped the call button (the pillar hero's secondary is 'How WCB physio works'), so doc and build disagree.
recommendation: Add an open question: is there a central line that can book WCB at any clinic? If yes, use it with aria-label 'Call Synergy Rehab bookings' and call tracking. If no, remove the pillar-level call CTA and give every finder row its own tel: link.

scope: Sticky bar: 6.1 band 12, section 10, Step 5 runbook
finding: The doc specifies only 'sticky bar on phones' and 'CSS only'. It does not address: (a) the LeadConnector chat bubble and GTranslate floating switcher, both loaded on the site (research/02 lines 220, 223), which sit in the bottom corners; design-system section 9.11 rates the collision LIKELY with selectors UNKNOWN, and the bar's call icon is bottom-right. (b) position:fixed fails under any Elementor/ElementsKit ancestor with transform, filter or will-change (motion effects, off-canvas menu), and the site runs GSAP and Lenis (design-system E3). (c) Hiding the bar over the hero needs animation-timeline and timeline-scope (worksafe.css line 621); in other browsers, and with reduced motion, the bar shows over the hero, so two primary CTAs are in view. (d) The pillar bar keeps saying 'Find your clinic' inside the 4,219 px finder, and at page end it covers about 72 px of the theme footer. (e) The location-page label 'Book online' names neither WCB nor the clinic (design-system rule 7 and section 13). (f) Step 5 post-publish checks do not include the bar.
recommendation: Make the sticky bar a launch gate: test on real iOS Safari and Android Chrome in the live theme. It must stay fixed to the viewport, stay hidden over the hero, and not be covered by chat, GTranslate or a cookie banner. Hide or move chat and GTranslate on WorkSafe URLs. Add named view timelines that hide the bar while #clinics and the final CTA band are in view. Change the label to 'Book WCB visit', with the clinic name in an sr-only span.

scope: Theme header on all WorkSafe pages (not mentioned in the doc)
finding: Every WorkSafe page inherits the global header 'BOOK NOW', which links to /booking-page/ (research/02 lines 97 and 143). It is a second primary CTA in the first view, which breaks the one-primary-CTA rule. It sends injured workers into the generic booking flow, where non-WCB and 'No Direct Billing' types are offered. The doc does not mention it, and its clicks are not measured.
recommendation: On /worksafe-physiotherapy/* and the guide, use an Elementor display condition to point the header CTA at #clinics (pillar) or at the clinic's 442 link (location pages), with a WCB label, or restyle it as secondary. Track its clicks as placement=header.

finding: The doc presents WCB massage at clinics where Jane shows it. But Jane offers only 'WCB Massage Subsequent Session - 30 minutes' (ID 21); there is no initial type (research/09 C-16). WSBC-35 requires a doctor's referral and an accepted claim, and RMT WorkSafeBC status per clinic is UNKNOWN (claims-register WSBC-35 notes; research/09 P-05). The built FAQ says 'WCB massage follow-up visits are bookable online at New Westminster'. SYN-01 covers the physiotherapy agreement only, so nothing gates this Synergy-specific claim.
recommendation: Add a per-clinic RMT claim (STAFF_CONFIRM) and an open question on how a worker books a first WCB massage visit. Until both are answered, leave massage off location pages. Once confirmed, use the CTA 'Call to book your first WCB massage visit' with the referral and accepted-claim requirement beside it. Never link to the Subsequent type in Jane.

scope: 6.1 title, meta and trust tiles (lines 181, 183, 187); band 8 (line 194)
finding: The brand rule is to say '19+ locations' exactly (design-system E1 and section 13). The title, meta description and trust tile say '19+ Clinics' or '19+ clinics', which the doc's own QA (line 333) would flag. 'Book ... at any of our 19+ locations' reads as WCB booking at more than 19 places, but Jane has exactly 19 WCB locations. '19+' is not in the claims register (research/09 P-07, C-10). The heading 'All 19 clinics' sits next to '19+'.
recommendation: Use '19+ locations' for brand mentions. State WCB availability with the gated count instead, for example 'WCB physio booking online at N locations'. Add the '19+ locations' brand claim to the register with a marketing sign-off.

finding: The coverage guide already ranks in 4 cities and is cited in AI Overviews (D3), so it will likely carry most WorkSafe traffic at launch. Yet section 6.3 gives it no CTA, sticky bar or finder, only 'link to pillar and finder'. Section 2 assigns pending-claim queries to the guide, but CUJ 2 lands that same query on the pillar FAQ. So the conversion path for pending-claim users is unspecified on the page that actually ranks.
recommendation: Give the guide and the RTW article: the pillar's sticky 'Find your clinic' bar, area chips or a compact finder after the pending-claim answer, the final CTA band, and page_type=guide/article events. Rewrite CUJ 2 to land on the guide, or change the ownership table.

finding: A 'hours today summary' cannot be computed in a static fragment, and section 10 rules out JavaScript. Putting hours in the meta description freezes them in search snippets. Hours come from the client-filled Yelp sheet, and Newton's conflict with GBP: Sat 8AM-7PM and Sun 8AM-4PM in the sheet vs Sat 08:00-16:00 and Sun 09:00-16:00 in GBP (locations-master.csv hours_gbp).
recommendation: Use a static weekly summary such as 'Open 7 days. Weekdays until 8:30 PM'. Require G2 sign-off on hours, and have qa-report flag any conflict between GBP and sheet hours.

scope: CTA copy across CUJ 1, 6.1, 6.2, sticky bar
finding: The same action carries five labels: 'Book a WCB initial assessment' (29 characters, over the 28-character rule), 'Book WCB assessment', 'Book WCB physio at Sullivan Heights' (35 characters, wraps to two lines at 390 px), 'Book online', and 'WorkSafe page' (vague, and conflicts with the section 8 anchor pattern '<Name> clinic').
recommendation: Use one family of labels, 28 characters or fewer, verb first, with the clinic name moved to an sr-only span when it would push the label over the limit. Use the section 8 anchor pattern for page links.

finding: The hero's in-page 'Find your clinic' anchor fires worksafe_location_select with clinic=all, which inflates that event. Finder clicks on pilot clinics count as location_select, not book_click, so pilot clinics will look worse on G-3. The doc does not specify GA4 cross-domain linking to janeapp.com, so Jane bookings cannot be attributed (forbidding hard-coded _gl is still correct). The site loads gtag three times (research/02 line 225).
recommendation: Use a separate event (worksafe_finder_open) for in-page anchors. Configure GA4 cross-domain linking for synergyrehab.janeapp.com so the linker decorates links on click. Dedupe the gtag loads before taking the day-30 baseline.

finding: Inter is LIKELY not loaded on the live site (design-system 5.1). The doc's performance budget ('one stylesheet of about 8 KB') and section 10 never decide how Inter is loaded. Without it, body text falls back to the system font and breaks the Montserrat/Inter brand rule.
recommendation: Decide on self-hosting Inter 400/600 as woff2 through Elementor Custom Fonts, include the font bytes in the budget, and verify fonts in the post-publish checks.

finding: The doc has no rule to show the web address as synergyrehab.ca, and design-system section 13 says whether synergyrehab.ca redirects cleanly is UNKNOWN.
recommendation: Add the copy rule (visible text synergyrehab.ca, hrefs to the canonical domain) and verify the redirect before the address is printed anywhere.

scope: NFR accessibility (line 291); finder and hours text
finding: Finder addresses and phones, the hours table and the proof line use 15 px (--sr-ws-fs-small). That is below 16 px for content the user needs in order to act. Breadcrumb targets are 29 px (design-system 9.13), while the NFR claims 48 px targets throughout.
recommendation: Raise task-critical text (address, phone, hours) to 16 px, and state the breadcrumb exception explicitly, or give breadcrumbs 48 px targets.

finding: worksafe.css sets no scroll-margin-top, so a sticky theme header can cover the target heading after an anchor jump (WCAG 2.4.11).
recommendation: Add .sr-ws-page [id]{scroll-margin-top: var(--header-offset, 88px)} and verify against the live header.

scope: 6.1 band 1 trust tiles and band 2 quick answers
finding: The trust tile 'evening and weekend hours' needs a qualifier: Clayton Corners is closed on weekends and Vancouver has no Saturday hours (worksafe-locations.json). The quick answer 'will I pay anything' tagged with WSBC-23 covers only accepted claims, but CUJ 2 users have pending claims, and a clinic may ask them to pay (WSBC-28; Synergy policy is Q-5).
recommendation: Write 'Evening and weekend hours at most locations'. Have the quick answer include the pending-claim case, or block it on Q-5 the same way the FAQ sentence is blocked.

scope: Consistency between 6.1/6.2, design-system 8.3 and the build
finding: The doc, the design system and the build disagree on: band order (steps are band 3 in the design system but inside band 4 in 6.2); a location-page sticky bar, which 6.2 omits; the pillar's secondary CTA; the location hero's 'WorkSafeBC contracted' badge (gated by SYN-01), which 6.2 omits. CUJ 3 promises WorkSafe pages for Surrey clinics, but none is in Wave 1. area_label values produce awkward H1s such as 'WorkSafeBC physiotherapy in King George Blvd, Surrey'.
recommendation: Make 6.1 and 6.2 the single source: list surfaces, the sticky bar and the badge with its claim gate. Align CUJ 3 with the wave plan. Set a display label per clinic for H1 use.

scope: §6.1 pillar (title, meta, bands 3 and 8), §4 gates, §6.2 band 7 nearby
finding: The publish gates cover location pages only. The pillar title and meta (lines 182-183), band 3 ("we handle WorkSafeBC billing") and band 8 (a Jane WCB booking link for every clinic without a page) advertise WorkSafeBC physio at all 19 clinics. Yet contract_2026 is UNVERIFIED for all 19 (worksafe-locations.json), and Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners are HIGH risk (merge_locations.py lines 24-25; §4 line 161 says publish only after Q-1). pages/dist/pillar/fragment.html already links janeapp cedar-hills and clayton-corners-188-st treatment/442. build_pages.mjs line 60 G1-gates SYN-01/SYN-08 only when a clinic object is passed, and the pillar passes none. Wave 1 nearby cards also link Jane WCB booking at Cedar Hills (from the New Westminster page) and Clayton Corners (from the Abbotsford page) (location.mjs lines 63-71). At a non-contracted clinic the worker pays and gets $95 back, paying the difference (WSBC-26).
recommendation: Gate the pillar and every nearby block on G1 per linked clinic. Clinics with G1 false get no WCB booking link and no WorkSafe wording (name, address and phone only, or omit them). The build computes N contracted clinics for the title, meta and finder heading instead of "19+". SYN-08 on the pillar requires G1 for every linked clinic.

scope: §9 Measurement, §10 WordPress delivery, NFR Security and privacy
finding: WorkSafe pages inherit sitewide trackers: GA4 gtag x3, Meta pixel x2 (1146132405487862, 993382379926498), CallTrackingMetrics, LeadConnector/GoHighLevel chat, CrazyEgg and Contentsquare (research/02 lines 223-225; research/01 line 254). §9's PIPA statement covers only custom event parameters. The page URL and the worksafe_* event names are themselves health and claim-status signals, sent to Meta and Google with identifiers. CTM links caller phone numbers to the pages they browsed and may record calls. The chat widget collects free text. spec/modern-seo-cluster.md line 34 extends the privacy rule to "ad tools", but the design drops that. §10 only says "must not add to these".
recommendation: Add a G6 Privacy gate before Wave 1. GTM blocking triggers exclude the Meta pixels, ad and remarketing tags, session replay and the chat widget on all WorkSafe URLs. Google signals and ad personalization are off for these pages, and there are no GA4/Ads/Meta audiences or conversion imports from worksafe_* events. CTM: no recording or transcription on these numbers, or a spoken notice. Identify the owners of the 3 GA4 properties. Update the privacy policy, and get privacy-officer sign-off.

finding: Known-wrong coverage copy stays live. SYN-03 (15 sessions / 6 weeks, CONFLICT) on /icbc-claims/ (343 footer in-links) is only an "Owner decision". On the King George and Delta clinic pages the fix waits "when each clinic page launches" (Wave 2, at least 30 days, line 163). SYN-04 ("Approved claims are eligible for treatment within 60 days", which the register flags as misleading at line 54) sits on /icbc-claims/ and the homepage (research/02 line 77; research/05 line 176) and is not in §3 at all. The homepage "No referral needed" anchor (SYN-06/WSBC-16 unconfirmed), the SYN-14 mileage blog claim and the 2023 15/6 social graphic are also omitted. G-4 counts only new pages.
recommendation: Correct every CONFLICT and DO_NOT_PUBLISH Synergy statement (SYN-02, 03, 04, 06, 11, 14) sitewide in week 1, whatever the wave. Make an explicit exception to the ICBC no-change rule for WorkSafe sentences on mixed pages. Extend G-4 to all site URLs.

finding: Cost answers are one-sided. CUJ 2 promises WorkSafeBC pays for the assessment even if the claim is denied. It omits that this depends on the clinic filing within 7 days (WSBC-29 notes), that pending-period follow-ups may be charged (WSBC-28, WSBC-30), and that Synergy's policy is unknown (Q-5, SYN-PEND placeholder). The pillar quick answer "Will I pay anything?" (pillar.mjs line 101) is WSBC-23 only. Non-claim body areas (WSBC-25) and any WCB no-show or cancellation fees (WSBC-24) are not addressed.
recommendation: Each cost answer states the accepted, pending and non-claim-area conditions in the same block. Make Q-5 a pillar launch blocker. Ops confirms no cancellation or no-show fees for WCB patients before "no fees" copy runs. Turn WSBC-29 into a Synergy commitment only if ops confirms it.

finding: Tag-only enforcement cannot meet G-4. Untagged Synergy claims: pillar.mjs line 76 ("any of our 19+ locations"), line 206 ("Every clinic below books WCB physio assessments online"), and line 144 ("Choose WCB Physio Initial Session so your first visit is set up as a WorkSafeBC claim", which is false because booking does not create a claim). Mis-tagging: line 28 tags "We explain what is approved for your claim" as SYN-05, whose register row (line 55) is about extension requests. build_pages.mjs claim() checks only the id's status, not the sentence. SYN-09 (no fees) is not in the G1 check on line 60.
recommendation: Add approved_wording per claim and have the build compare the tagged text against it. Lint for untagged coverage terms (WorkSafeBC/WCB with pay, fee, bill, claim, visits, referral, approved). G1-gate every SYN-* claim. Delete the "set up as a claim" tip.

scope: §6.1 band 9, §6.2 band 3, §2 massage and acupuncture row
finding: WCB massage (9 clinics) and acupuncture (Nordel) are promoted on Jane bookability alone. G1 covers only the physio agreement. The register says bookability is not proof of a contract (SYN-JANE, line 70), per-clinic RMT contract status is UNKNOWN (WSBC-35, line 36), and the acupuncturist's status needs confirming (WSBC-36, line 37). Jane offers only "WCB Massage Subsequent", which still needs a referral and an accepted claim.
recommendation: Add per-clinic massage and acupuncture contract gates in worksafe-locations.json. Show those services and keywords only where confirmed. Otherwise leave out the band and the FAQ answer.

finding: §9 suggests turning on Jane's analytics integration with no limits. research/01 line 189 shows footer Jane links carrying _gl/_ga, so GA4 cross-domain linking is likely configured. gtag will decorate clean hrefs at click time, so "no _gl strings" in the authored HTML does not prevent WorkSafe sessions being joined to Jane bookings, where the appointment type ("WCB Physio Initial Session") reveals claim status. A Meta pixel on Jane would disclose that to Meta.
recommendation: State explicitly: no Meta or ad pixels in Jane. If GA4 is used in Jane, send only a generic booking_complete event, with no treatment or practitioner names. Review the cross-domain settings for janeapp.com. Make this part of the G6 privacy sign-off.

scope: Detailed plan Step 1 (collector data), repo hygiene
finding: README line 8 tells you to make the collector repo public. origin/data:availability.json holds 14,831 rows of practitioners' full names with their open appointment times, refreshed about every 2 minutes. That is employee/contractor personal information republished in machine-readable form. worksafe-seo/ (eligibility-risk notes, GBP metrics, the marketing email repeated hundreds of times) is pushed to the same remote. No patient fields were found (fields: location, service, treatment, practitioner, duration, datetime, booking_url). merge_locations.py uses names only to count them.
recommendation: Make the repo private, or drop or hash practitioner names before publishing the data branch (counts are enough). Move the research to a private repo. Confirm with Jane that automated collection of the booking site fits Synergy's agreement.

scope: §6.2 band 5 WCB team, Q-7, Q-9, NFR photos
finding: Consent gaps. There is no process to withdraw consent or remove departed staff. CHCPBC registration checks exist only as an ASSUMPTION (design-system line 539). The "focus" field can read as a claimed specialty. The heading "WCB physiotherapists" suggests a WorkSafeBC credential, but WorkSafeBC contracts clinics. The pillar hero alt text "physiotherapist assessing a patient's shoulder" (pillar.mjs line 84) means a recognisable person is implied to be an injured worker. The Drive photos were never opened and some folders share stock images (design-system line 751). The reviewer line names a PT without a consent rule.
recommendation: Use a written consent form naming WorkSafe-page use, with a withdrawal path and a quarterly roster check against Jane. Verify each card against the CHCPBC register. Use staff or consenting models, never actual patients. Label the band "Physiotherapists who treat WorkSafeBC claims". Get the reviewer's consent too.

finding: The pillar owns "wcb approved physiotherapy" (line 112), and keyword-master rows 8, 10, 50-53 and 107-109 carry "approved" variants. WorkSafeBC contracts providers; it does not approve or endorse them. Synergy's Yelp listing already says "WCB and WorkSafeBC Approved Physiotherapy" (research/08 lines 411, 592), and Medimap omits WCB (SYN-16). Neither is in §3.
recommendation: Ban "approved" and "endorsed" wording and any WorkSafeBC logo in copy, titles and badges. Use "WorkSafeBC-contracted" only after G1. Add the third-party listing corrections (Yelp, Medimap) to §3, to run after SYN-01.

finding: The "Facts checked against worksafebc.com on <date>" line can publish when only checked_as_of and reviewer are set (build_pages.mjs line 99). OK_TO_PUBLISH rows were verified from search snippets, and nothing records that each was opened. SOURCES.providers (shared.mjs line 14) is the URL the register (WSBC-33) says never surfaced, so a cited source link may be broken.
recommendation: Add a per-claim opened_on date in claims-signoff.json for every claim used, including OK_TO_PUBLISH rows, and refuse publish without it. Replace the providers URL with a verified one.

finding: In CUJ 1 the worker has not reported to WorkSafeBC and books from the hero. The report step is one scroll below. The location hero lede (location.mjs line 83) never says report first. WSBC-13 notes that no source says a clinic may assess a worker who has not reported, so the booking may not be billable.
recommendation: Put a reporting line beside the hero CTA (report online or call 1.888.967.5377; your claim can be pending). Add an ops question on how unreported WCB bookings are handled and charged.

scope: §2 RTW row, §6.3 RTW article, design-system band 6
finding: The RTW article targets "return to work program". WSBC-40 (line 41) says do not imply Synergy runs the Customized Recovery and RTW Program, and Synergy is not on the RTWSS list. WSBC-39 says there is no stand-alone WorkSafeBC kinesiology benefit. design-system line 345 plans "Return-to-work services here (kinesiology on site)", which conflicts with both.
recommendation: Add a content rule to §6.3. WorkSafeBC RTW programs and RTWSS are separate and need approved providers, and Synergy does not deliver them unless confirmed. Mention kinesiology only as KIN support sessions inside the physio treatment period, after WSBC-39 is confirmed.

finding: Q-4 asks staff to "confirm" WSBC-16, but the register (line 17) says no official source states it and recommends WSBC-10 wording. The pillar quick answer is the absolute "Not for physiotherapy."
recommendation: Use WSBC-10 wording ("WorkSafeBC tells workers to go straight to a contracted physiotherapist"), or require an official citation, not just a staff sign-off.

finding: Jane offerings are a 2026-11-02 snapshot. The build has no maximum age on wcb_data_checked_at. Massage and acupuncture "bookable" is inferred from open slots in one 7-day window (merge_locations.py lines 43-50), not from the treatment catalogue, so it can change with schedules.
recommendation: Fail publish if the Jane data is older than 7 days. Derive offerings from Jane's treatment list, not from open slots.

finding: The stack includes Widget Google Reviews and WP Google Places Review Slider (research/02 line 224), which copy testimonials onto pages. Nothing keeps them off WorkSafe templates. research/08 line 547 suggests replying to reviews and mentioning WorkSafeBC, but there is no rule against confirming patient or claim status.
recommendation: Confirm the widgets never render on WorkSafe URLs, and check against CHCPBC advertising limits on testimonials. Add a reply rule: never confirm that a reviewer is a patient or has a WorkSafeBC claim.

finding: The committed preview fragments render "WorkSafeBC contracted" for all 19 clinics, including HIGH-risk Cedar Hills, marked only with a dashed outline.
recommendation: In preview mode, render pending SYN-01 as "Contract status: staff to confirm" rather than the final badge text.

finding: There is no test plan. The build script is the only thing that enforces G-4 (accuracy) and gates G1-G5, yet the plan names no test cases, fixtures, runner or assertions, which the standard requires. The build also starts with fs.rmSync(OUT), so ad-hoc test runs against the real data delete pages/dist.
recommendation: Add build/test/build_pages.test.mjs using node:test, plus a --root/--data/--out flag so tests run on fixture data. Required cases: DO_NOT_PUBLISH id -> exit 1 and page skipped; unsigned STAFF_CONFIRM -> blocked in publish, pending marker in preview; SYN-01/SYN-08 with G1 false -> blocked; any gate false -> skipped with the gate list; G3 3/7 blocked and 4/7 passes; em/en dash blocked; 66-character title blocked; unknown claim id blocked; another clinic's Jane slug blocked; checked_as_of null blocks the pillar; missing hero photo blocked; all-pass fixture writes 4 files per page plus qa-report.json.

finding: Step 2 says to create pages/src/pillar.html and location.template.html with {{...}} slots and conditional blocks. The repo already has pages/src/pillar.mjs, location.mjs and shared.mjs (JS template functions imported by build_pages.mjs); nothing reads .html templates and no slot syntax is defined. The committed titles also differ from §6.1 and §6.2 (code: 'WCB & WorkSafeBC Physio in ${place} | Synergy Rehab'). coverage-guide.html and return-to-work.html do not exist, are not rendered by Step 3, and have no title, H1, meta, outline, claim mapping or delivery format.
recommendation: Rewrite Step 2 to match the .mjs modules: name the exported functions and the ctx API (claim, slot, photo, team, asof, linked, href). State whether §6 titles and H1s or the code is authoritative. For the coverage guide and the RTW article, add full page specs (title, H1, meta, H2 list, claim ids per H2, word range, JSON-LD, source module, build output) or declare them hand-written outside the build, with an owner.

finding: There is no rollout phase or publish sequence. The pillar fragment already links /return-to-work-after-a-workplace-injury/ twice, a new URL with no requirement to go live first, so it 404s. With --link published, pillar finder and sibling nearby links follow JSON gates at build time, not live WordPress status. Publishing or rolling back one clinic requires re-pasting the pillar and several siblings, which is never stated. The pillar has no gates and no publish criteria.
recommendation: Add Phase 6 'Wave rollout': (1) publish the guide refresh and the RTW article; (2) publish the Wave 1 location pages; (3) rebuild and re-paste the pillar with --link published; (4) rebuild and re-paste the affected siblings; (5) run post-publish checks. Add a rollback procedure: gate false, rebuild, re-paste the pillar and siblings, then set the page to draft. Define pillar publish preconditions.

finding: Step 1.1 is marked done, but the merge rewrites staff_facts (all null) and publish_gates (G4 true, others false) on every run, wiping the hand edits that CUJ 4 relies on. It needs an undocumented availability.json argument from origin/data. 16 of 76 nearby entries were mis-parsed (e.g. '8056 King George Blvd, Surrey ; 03 Central City', slug null) and are silently dropped by location.mjs, so 15 pages show fewer than the 4 nearby clinics §6.2 requires (Newton shows 2). There is no acceptance criterion.
recommendation: Split the data into a generated file and a hand-maintained overlay (e.g. data/worksafe-staff.json for staff_facts, gates and NAP overrides) that the merge never touches. Document the exact merge command and input. Fix the km_list regex. Add a check that every clinic has 4 nearby entries with non-null slugs, sorted by km.

finding: The questionnaire columns are not defined ('Q-6 and Q-7 fields') and no ingestion path exists. The template uses slot 'check_in', which is not in the merge schema or the G3 list. The wcb_team_with_consent item shape is undefined. Photos are split: staff_facts.photo_with_consent counts toward G3 but is never rendered, while photos.json keys <slug>_hero/<slug>_inside are rendered and block publish but do not count toward G3. photos.json is not mentioned in the plan, including Step 3.1's input list.
recommendation: Give the exact CSV header (every staff_facts key, NAP fields, consent flags, photo id, signer and date). Add an ingestion script that writes the overlay. Define the wcb_team_with_consent item schema {name, credential, focus, languages[]}. Make one photo field the source of truth and count it in G3.

finding: The schema has one global checked_as_of, so it cannot record the per-URL check dates §5 requires for every cited official URL. SYN-01 and SYN-08 are per-clinic facts, but sign-off is keyed by claim id only. The pillar calls claim('SYN-08') with no clinic, so G1 never applies: once SYN-08 is signed globally, the pillar states 'we handle WorkSafeBC billing' for all 19 clinics, including Cedar Hills and Clayton Corners (HIGH risk, G1 false).
recommendation: Add sources: {url: {checked, by}} and block any claim whose official_source_url has no entry. Make SYN-01 and SYN-08 per clinic or derive them only from G1. Define the pillar rule, e.g. SYN-08 wording only when every finder clinic has G1 true, or qualified wording.

finding: Publish-mode failure behaviour is undefined (whole build vs per page; the code skips per page and exits 1, CUJ 4 says it 'stops'). The output path is wrong: publish writes to pages/publish/, not pages/dist/. 'Any empty required slot' names no slots, and the code strips empty slots instead of blocking. G3 exists as both a manual flag and a computed count. The --markers and --link flags are undocumented. The plan says em dash; the code also rejects en dashes.
recommendation: State the exact failure contract and the output directory per mode, list the required slots per template, make G3 either computed or manual (not both), and document all CLI flags with their defaults.

finding: 'Unique-text ratio' is undefined. The code reports max 5-word-shingle Jaccard (current values 0.418-0.530) with no pass/fail threshold. In publish mode the comparison set is only the gate-passing pages (2 others in Wave 1), so the value is not comparable. The manual band-removal test appears in no step.
recommendation: Define the metric, with the shared footer and sources excluded; always compare against all 19 preview renders; set a hard publish threshold (e.g. 0.35 or lower); add the band-removal review with a named reviewer to Step 4.

finding: The overflow check runs only at 390 and 1280 (320 and 768 are required, and no tool is named for them). screenshot.mjs always exits 0. QA reads only pages/dist preview output, never the publish output that is pasted. The Jane-slug rule cannot hold on the pillar or nearby cards, and the code checks only membership. The tel: rule fails on the Teleclaim link +18889675377 and is not implemented. The '19+ locations' rule is undefined and conflicts with '19+ Clinics' in the §6.1 title and meta. The NFR checks (LCP, CLS, 48 px targets; the script counts targets under 24 px; WCAG contrast) have no step.
recommendation: Create build/qa.mjs --dir pages/publish with exit codes and viewports 320/390/768/1280. Precise link rules: hero/booking links use the page clinic's slug, finder/nearby links use the card clinic's slug, tel: equals phone_e164 or Teleclaim. Define the 19+ wording rule. Add Lighthouse mobile thresholds and a 48 px tap-target assertion.

finding: The WordPress steps leave design decisions open: page parent (location pages must be children of /worksafe-physiotherapy/ to get the planned URLs), which SEO plugin (unidentified in research/01), how JSON-LD is inserted and how it avoids clashing with the plugin's graph, how CSS is enqueued only on WorkSafe URLs (and where the file lives), how to suppress the second auto-generated meta description and canonical that research/01 says new pages inherit, and how to noindex /tag/worksafebc/.
recommendation: Decide each item in the spec and write the exact admin path or code snippet into the runbook (e.g. a child-theme wp_enqueue_scripts hook with an is_page/parent check; Page Attributes > Parent = WorkSafe Physiotherapy; the named SEO plugin field for title, meta and robots).

scope: Lines 319-320, 337 (Step 2 markup, Step 5 GTM); shared.mjs ev()
finding: No step requires the data-sr-event attributes or defines their contract. §9 names the parameter clinic_slug, but the code emits data-clinic (value 'all' on the pillar hero), data-placement and data-page-type. The GTM trigger, variables and GA4 tag are only 'GTM triggers' in the runbook. §9 says names may change after GA4 access, with no re-mapping step.

finding: No step builds the G5 tracking set: URL Target is 'Not Available' on all 508 keyword-master rows, and the ~121 keyword pairs and 10 AI prompts exist in no file. finding: The massage and acupuncture conditions are undefined. The data flags mean 'had an open slot in one 7-day snapshot' (availability.json, 2026-11-02T07:31Z), so a fully booked clinic loses the band. There is no step to refresh the data before publishing.

finding: Steps 2 and 3 plan files that already exist in HEAD 1b0caad, in a different form. finding: The plan says publish 'fails on any empty required slot'. The code does not: slot() returns '' and only records the field in `missing`, and line 212 strips the empty rows. finding: Any unsigned STAFF_CONFIRM claim blocks the whole page. scope: design_draft.md line 333; build/screenshot.mjs lines 13-19; build_pages.mjs lines 182-189; location.mjs line 187
finding: Most Step 4.2 checks are missing or unassigned. The 320 and 768 px widths are never captured. finding: screenshot.mjs captures the pillar and Wave 1 by default, not 'each preview', and writes both full-page and -fold PNGs. It swallows load errors, so a missing page gives a blank screenshot. It reads only pages/dist, so it shows preview markers rather than publish output. Playwright resolves only through the environment's NODE_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH; the repo has no node_modules.
recommendation: Specify the page list, the install step (npm install at the repo root or the required env vars), failing on load errors, and which output folder is captured.

scope: design_draft.md line 313; merge_locations.py lines 4, 43-50, 74-77; collect.js header (data branch force-pushed every 2 min)
finding: WCB massage and acupuncture 'bookable' means an open slot appeared in the collector's 8-day window of an unpinned, force-pushed data-branch snapshot, and the plan gives no command to fetch it. A busy week can switch a clinic's massage content off. Treatment 442 is hardcoded rather than checked per clinic; other ids exist (948, 968, 1013, 1019, 1081).
recommendation: Commit a dated snapshot or record its commit SHA, document the command (git show origin/data:availability.json), base 'bookable' on the type catalogue rather than openings, and check 442 per clinic.

scope: design_draft.md lines 320, 327 vs §6.1, §6.2, §7; location.mjs lines 7-21; pillar.mjs lines 4-10; build_pages.mjs lines 108-139
finding: Steps 2-3 rely on §6 and §7, but the code differs. The location title is 'WCB & WorkSafeBC Physio in <place> | Synergy Rehab' (fallback above 62 characters) instead of the §6.2 pattern. The pillar title and location meta differ from the spec, and the pillar hero has no call button. The Organization schema lacks logo and telephone, and dateModified and hasMap are missing.
recommendation: State which source is authoritative and list the exact title, meta and schema rules the build must follow.

finding: There is no test plan, and the repo has no tests or fixtures for the gating logic (DO_NOT_PUBLISH, unsigned STAFF_CONFIRM, G1 false with SYN-01, empty slot, dash, title length, unknown claim id).
recommendation: Add specific happy-path and edge-case tests with fixture data, and the command that runs them.

finding: No step has a verification command or exit criterion, so the standard's phasing and checkpoint rule is not met, and there is no npm script for the build.
recommendation: Give each step a command and an expected result, e.g. `node worksafe-seo/build/build_pages.mjs --mode preview` exits 0 with 20 pages built.

finding: The RUNBOOK step leaves decisions open. The SEO plugin is not identified anywhere. schema.json is raw JSON with no rule for wrapping it in a script tag. The way to load the CSS only on WorkSafe pages is not given. The stylesheet is 59,033 B raw and 11,422 B gzipped, against the ~8 KB min+gzip requirement, with no minify step. The GTM triggers need container access the project does not have.
recommendation: Name the SEO plugin (or a step to identify it), the JSON-LD wrapping, the CSS loading method, a minify step in the build, and who configures GTM.

finding: The dash check misses — and — entities, and it also rejects en dashes, which the plan does not mention.
recommendation: Include entity forms in the check and document the en-dash rule.

finding: The 'as of' wording differs from §5 ('Facts checked against worksafebc.com on <date>' vs 'Facts checked against WorkSafeBC sources as of <date>. Reviewed by <name, PT>'), and the preview fallback hardcodes 'Sources researched November 2, 2026'.
recommendation: Pick one wording and use it in both the spec and the code.

finding: Skipped pages leave empty pages/publish/<id>/ folders, and the plan does not say that pages/publish is gitignored.
recommendation: Create the folder only after the checks pass, and document that publish output is not committed.

finding: yelp[jane] raises an uncaught KeyError if a clinic is missing from yelp-nap.csv.
recommendation: Check that all inputs are present and fail with a clear message.

finding: The content of REPORT.md's '10 next actions' is not specified.
recommendation: List the actions, or say which open questions they come from.

finding: "pages/dist/<page>/fragment.html (paste into WordPress)" is true only for preview mode. Publish mode writes to pages/publish/. The current pages/dist fragments hold "Staff to confirm" boxes (7 in richmond) and pending-claim title attributes, so following the instruction publishes placeholder text.
recommendation: Give the output directory for each mode. Make pages/publish/<page>/fragment.html the only paste source. Label pages/dist/ "preview only, never paste".

finding: The text names pages/src/pillar.html and location.template.html with {{...}} slots and a {{finder}} placeholder. The repo has pillar.mjs, location.mjs and shared.mjs (JS template functions, no {{ tokens). "Using design-system components" is vague, and an article is missing ("and {{finder}} placeholder").
recommendation: Name the real modules and their exports. Describe the mechanism as ctx.claim(id, html) adding data-claim to each fact. Cite spec/design-system.md §4-§9.

finding: The mode description is wrong. The label is "Staff to confirm:", not "STAFF TO CONFIRM", and pending claims are dashed outlines, not boxes. The --markers and --link flags are undocumented. The sentence switches nouns (clinics vs pages; the pillar has no gates). "Fails on" is ambiguous (the build skips the page and exits 1). "Required slot" is undefined (the build blocks only when fewer than 4 of 7 G3 facts are filled or the hero photo is missing). The build also rejects en dashes, long titles and meta descriptions, an H1 count other than 1, a missing "19+ locations" and unknown Jane slugs. The input list leaves out data/photos.json and worksafe.css.
recommendation: Replace the sentence with a list of publish blockers that matches build_pages.mjs one for one. Document both flags. Complete the input list.

finding: "Unique-text ratio" is undefined and has no threshold. The build computes max_similarity: the highest 5-word-shingle Jaccard score against the most similar other location page, which runs the opposite way to a uniqueness ratio. The listed qa-report fields (H1, internal links) do not exist, and the real fields (pending_claims, missing_staff_facts, issues, most_similar_to) are not listed.
recommendation: Name the metric exactly. Set a pass threshold or name who sets it. List the report fields by their real keys.

finding: "QA checks:" is a verbless list with no actor or method. It repeats checks the build already enforces (em dash, Jane slug, similarity). It lists checks nothing implements: tel: matching, JSON-LD parsing, and scroll checks at 320 and 768 px (screenshot.mjs checks only 390 and 1280). "Reported" is not a pass condition.
recommendation: Split the list into "Enforced by build_pages.mjs" and "screenshot.mjs or manual", naming the tool for each check. Remove the duplicates. Give each item a verb and a pass condition.

finding: "The Q-6 and Q-7 fields" points at prose questions, not field lists. Q-7 leaves out "nearby workplaces served", which G3 and staff_facts.nearby_workplaces require, so the questionnaire would lack a G3 column.
recommendation: List the CSV columns by key: the NAP fields plus the 7 staff_facts keys.

finding: The sources are named in undefined jargon ("collector's public data branch", "client-filled Yelp list", "ICBC page data", "GBP fields where known"). One attribution is wrong: Jane slugs are hard-coded in merge_locations.py CLINICS, and the location id comes from locations-master.csv. The item is one 70-word sentence with a nine-part inline list.
recommendation: Replace it with a two-column table (output field, source file) using repo paths: data/yelp-nap.csv, research/02-icbc-location-pages.csv, data/locations-master.csv, origin/data availability.json.

finding: Only Step 1.1 is marked done. Step 1.2 says "Add" a claims-signoff.json that already exists, with a _how_to_use key the stated schema does not show. The outputs of Steps 3 and 4 (build_pages.mjs, screenshot.mjs, 20 dist folders, 8 PNGs) exist with no status. A reader cannot tell what remains.
recommendation: Give every item a status and date, or remove status from the plan and track it in PROJECT-STATE.md.

finding: The "19+ locations" wording check has no verb and does not say whether it tests presence, exactness or exclusivity. The build tests presence only. §6.1 specifies "19+ Clinics", "19+ Synergy Rehab clinics" and "19+ clinics", while design-system.md line 699 requires "19+ locations" exactly. The document breaks the rule it checks.
recommendation: State the rule as: every page contains the exact string "19+ locations" and no other location-count wording. Align the §6.1 strings.

finding: "Captures each preview" is inaccurate. By default the script captures the pillar and the 3 Wave 1 pages, each as a full-page and a first-screen shot. "Pre-installed Chromium" describes the environment, not the plan.
recommendation: "Captures the pillar and Wave 1 previews by default (other page ids by argument) at 390 px and 1280 px, full page and first screen, into previews/."

finding: The RUNBOOK and REPORT paths carry a worksafe-seo/ prefix. Every other path in the scope is relative to worksafe-seo/.
recommendation: Drop the prefix, or state the base directory once at the top of the section.

finding: One 75-word item packs in two nested parenthetical lists. Its post-publish checks ("live URL 200", "canonical", "rendered meta") name a topic, not an expected result, although §10 records duplicate canonicals and meta descriptions on the site.
recommendation: Use sub-bullets with one expected result each, for example "exactly one rel=canonical, equal to the page URL; exactly one meta description".

finding: "10 next actions" is a fixed count with no rationale. "Executive summary" does not say what it contains.
recommendation: "A prioritised list of next actions, each with owner and blocking question (Q-n)."

finding: "Article bodies" does not say who writes them, and §6.3 sends the coverage guide to the content owner as a separate file. "For each page" suggests the build renders the articles, but build_pages.mjs renders only the pillar and the 19 location pages.
recommendation: State that the build does not render the coverage guide or the RTW article, and name who writes and signs off each one.
